articles.title: IFA Shield final: East Bengal & Mohun Bagan resume rivalry with bruised ego and another title up for grabs
articles.summary: Kolkata: After playing host to India’s unprecedented brush with full-strength Brazil and Uruguay in two Fifa friendlies, it’s time for normal service to
articles.body: Kolkata: After playing host to India’s unprecedented brush with full-strength Brazil and Uruguay in two Fifa friendlies, it’s time for normal service to resume in the city’s traditional football-scape.East Bengal FC and Mohun Bagan SG will return to the refurbished Salt Lake Stadium for another derby on Thursday — the fourth one between them across tournaments so far in this season and with the IFA Shield title now up for grabs.A year ago, Mohun Bagan edged their arch-rivals on penalties in the final. However, for the defending champions, it’s the memories of another final, held at the same venue one-and-an-half month ago, which seem to be more on their mind than anything else.Panagiotis Dilmperis began his stint with Bagan with a derby win in the Durand Cup but East Bengal — also under a new coach in Antonio Lopez Habas — settled the score when it mattered most, brushing them aside 4-1 in the final.That Aug 23 scoreline in the Durand final was put on the table during the teams’ pre-match news conferences at a city hotel on Wednesday and both coaches approached them with their own perspectives.“It's a derby. It's a game for our ego, our reputation and for our fans. At least we should do our best. And when the game is finished, we shouldn't put up an excuse that we’ve not given our best and done our job properly and without heart,” Panagiotis told reporters.“We are ready, 100% ready for the final. We are preparing to play a different match, a match absolutely different than the last final (in Durand Cup),” Habas made his mind clear.The two teams’ road to the final is also different. While Mohun Bagan had to rely on goalkeeper Vishal Kaith’s heroics to get past Punjab FC in the semifinal, East Bengal blew away NorthEast United FC 7-2 on the back of David Lalhlansanga’s hat-trick to ensure the repeat of last year’s final.Both teams are expected to go full throttle against each other welcoming their respective national players back in the fold. Panagiotis hopes that the arrival of Anirudh Thapa, who scored against Uruguay, Manvir Singh and Apuia will provide his tea with a new stability and dimension.Habas, on the other hand, will take a late call on the availability of the likes of defender Anwar Ali, Jay Gupta, midfielder Jeakson Singh and goalkeeper Prabhsukhan Gill.Highlighting the need of “coordinating” the India players with new overseas signing like Ake Loba and Lukasz Zwolinski, the East Bengal coach decided to opt for a closed-door training session at their home ground.A year ago in the Shield final, then East Bengal coach Oscar Bruzon took a gamble of replacing Gill with Debjit Majumdar but it didn’t pay off as Bagan stayed perfect in the shootout while Kaith saved Jay Gupta’s attempt to clinch the deal.As the rivalry reappears, Habas is keen on avoiding such setback in a shootout. “For me, I prefer to win the final in 90 minutes,” the East Bengal coach said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Kolkata: “They (the players) deserve that at least,” head coach Crispin Chettri said of fans coming to watch the Indian women’s team play their first-ever
articles.body: Kolkata: “They (the players) deserve that at least,” head coach Crispin Chettri said of fans coming to watch the Indian women’s team play their first-ever international match, albeit unofficial, at Salt Lake Stadium here on Thursday.Indeed, with the frenzy surrounding the men’s team’s marquee friendlies against Brazil and Uruguay, it’s time for the 69th-ranked Indians to take on world No. 27 Russia in a return to action after their SAFF Championship triumph in June.“I think playing against higher-ranked teams is always good for us because we want to develop as a football nation, and we learn not only what is done on the field, but also how it is done off the field,” Chettri said after a training session at the venue on Wednesday.It also gives India an opportunity to expose youngsters to international football and start building a squad with the 2029 AFC Women’s Asian Cup in mind.“We have a very young side. articles.title: 'You earned that love': Lionel Messi's wife Antonela Roccuzzo pays emotional tribute
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi’s final game for Argentina turned into an emotional farewell in Buenos Aires, with his wife Antonela Roccuzzo sharing a heartfelt
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi’s final game for Argentina turned into an emotional farewell in Buenos Aires, with his wife Antonela Roccuzzo sharing a heartfelt message for the football superstar after his international career came to an end.Messi scored a penalty and set up Argentina’s other two goals as they beat Benin 3-0 on Tuesday. Soon after the match, Roccuzzo took to Instagram to celebrate the love Messi received from the Argentine fans.“There are nights that explain a whole life. And last night was one of those. How beautiful it was to see you surrounded by so much love, so many people thanking you and giving back everything you gave them for so many years. You earned that love. You built it with your personality, your humility, your commitment, and the heart you always gave for this jersey," Messi's wife Antonela wrote."What a privilege to have walked this path by your side and what a thrill to see you close such a huge chapter of your life in this way. Thank you for teaching us so much! We love you! @leomessi. Always with you,” she said.Messi’s 21-year Argentina journey endsThe 39-year-old brought the curtain down on a 21-year international career with 126 goals and 208 appearances for Argentina.His list of major honours includes two Copa América titles and the 2022 World Cup.What was officially a friendly against Benin became a huge farewell event, with more than 85,000 supporters turning up at Buenos Aires' biggest stadium.The Argentine Football Federation promoted the match as “the last tango”. Former World Cup winners from Argentina’s 1978, 1986 and 2022 teams were also present to witness Messi’s final appearance.As the match ended, Messi was visibly emotional while his teammates surrounded him. The stadium erupted into chants of “Olé, olé, olé, olé, Messi, Messi”, while a banner at midfield called him the "Eternal Captain.”“The truth is, I'm talking more than I ever have. I don't want to leave here, I don't want to leave this field,” Messi told the crowd, which roared as if he had scored. “I just want to tell you that I love you, I'm going to miss you, and I'm grateful to God to be Argentine."From criticism to becoming Argentina’s heroMessi’s journey with Argentina was not always filled with praise.For years, some supporters questioned his commitment to the national team because he moved from Rosario to Spain at 13 and developed as a footballer at Barcelona.His calm personality was also compared with the more outspoken character of Diego Maradona, who led Argentina to the 1986 World Cup title.After Argentina suffered another major final defeat in 2016, Messi briefly stepped away from international football.His relationship with the fans changed significantly in 2021 when Argentina defeated Brazil to win the Copa América. Messi’s emotional reaction after the triumph became one of the defining moments of his international career.“Winning clearly disarmed his critics. That's how soccer works in Argentina,” said Diego Murzi, a sports sociologist at Conicet, Argentina's national scientific research council. “Criticism of things off the field goes hand in hand with defeats on it.”The following year, Messi finally lifted the World Cup in Qatar. The victory ended Argentina’s long wait and cemented his place among the country’s greatest sporting heroes.“I'll never forget it. I'd never experienced anything like that, being out there with everyone, celebrating together,” said Antonia Correa, 70, a kiosk owner, recalling that day as she waited for a bus in Buenos Aires on Tuesday. “We saw that he wasn't just an extraordinary player, but an excellent human being.”‘A love story’ with ArgentinaBy the end of his international career, the relationship between Messi and Argentina had transformed completely.“I don't know if there has ever been a love story between a player and a nation as great as the one you built,” his teammate Rodrigo De Paul wrote on Instagram.For many Argentines, Messi became much more than a footballer. His biggest victories gave the country moments of happiness during years of political and economic difficulties.“Argentines often say, Thank God I was born at a time when I could experience the miracle of watching Messi play,'” said Andrés Rabinovich, a University of Chicago scholar who has researched soccer's role in Argentine culture. “It's hard living in Argentina. Soccer is often one of the few things that offers you some respite, some joy.”Messi will now continue his club career with Inter Miami.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lucía Corrales: autopista hasta Brasil
articles.standfirst: La balear, que vive su segunda temporada en el London City Lionesses, es una de las grandes apuestas de Sonia Bermúdez
articles.summary: La balear, que vive su segunda temporada en el London City Lionesses, es una de las grandes apuestas de Sonia Bermúdez
articles.body: La banda zurda de la selección española tiene dueña para esta ventana internacional: Lucía Corrales. La futbolista balear, actualmente en el London City Lionesses, es una de las fijas para Sonia Bermúdez desde su llegada al banquillo de la absoluta, donde ya suma ocho internacionalidades y un gol. "Cada partido con la selección es único para mí, pero evidentemente poder jugar contra Estados Unidos, una de las mejores selecciones del mundo, con un nivel altísimo, supone un plus de motivación", asegura en MARCA la protagonista antes del doble compromiso ante la actual campeona olímpica. Tras ser subcampeona de Europa y campeona del mundo con la Sub'17 y campeona de Europa con la Sub'19, Corrales debutó con la selección absoluta el 30 de mayo de 2025 ante Bélgica. "Me he sentido súper a gusto siempre que he tenido la oportunidad de jugar. Creo que tengo la confianza de Sonia, a la que ya conocía de las categorías inferiores, y de mis compañeras dentro del campo. A muchas las conocía de mi etapa en el Barça, a otras de la selección, ... Creo que el nivel es tan alto que es importante estar bien cuando te toca y pienso que a mí me ha ido bien. No me conformo con eso y seguiré trabajando para que vengan muchos más partidos", sostiene. El nombre de Lucía ha aparecido en las listas de convocadas tanto en la nómina de defensas como en la de delanteras. ¿Dónde se siente más cómoda Corrales? "En la izquierda, eso seguro", regatea. "Siempre he sido extremo, pero ahora estoy jugando más de lateral tanto en la selección como en el equipo. En ambas posiciones me siento cómoda. En ambos modelos de juego tengo la posibilidad de poder subir mucho a posiciones más ofensivas, que es algo que a mí me gusta, así que disfruto mucho en ese carril", justifica. La talentosa futbolista balear pertenece a la generación de 2005, la misma que Vicky López, Sara Ortega, Carla Camacho o Paula Partido entre otras. "El fútbol en España se está trabajando muy bien. Mira los resultados de la selección en categorías inferiores. Hay muchísimas jugadoras jóvenes con muchísimo talento. A todas nos viene muy bien que haya niñas que vengan por detrás empujando fuerte; te hace estar siempre concentrada y no perder la chispa", resume. El Mundial de Brasil, que se disputará del 24 de junio al 25 de julio de 2027, es uno de los sueños por cumplir para Corrales. "A todas nos encantaría poder estar en el Mundial representando a España. Es una cosa súper bonita, pero la temporada es muy larga y pueden pasar miles de cosas. Soy de las que piensa que una siempre tiene que estar preparada por lo que pueda llegar... Ojalá no tenga vacaciones en julio", asevera. "Acaba de empezar la temporada y las selecciones empezamos a preparar el Mundial. Creo que aún es pronto para hablar de favoritas", subraya. La competencia por el puesto de lateral izquierdo es, a día de hoy, muy elevada: Olga Carmona, Andrea Medina, Nerea Nevado, Leila Ouahabi, Alejandra Bernabé... "Soy un poco pasota en ese aspecto. No miro lo que hacen mis compañeras, sino que simplemente me centro en mi juego y en el de mi equipo. Supongo que habrá gente que igual lo haga porque le venga bien a su rendimiento, pero yo prefiero pasar. Tenemos muchísimas cosas en las que pensar, pero cuanto más competencia haya será mejor para todas", sentencia. Criada en las canteras del Collerense y Atlético Baleares, Lucía dio el salto al Barcelona con 16 años, donde estuvo tres temporadas -llegando a debutar con el primer equipo- antes de salir cedida al Sevilla y traspasada al London City Lionesses en 2025. "Cambiar de país requiere una adaptación, pero creo que el año pasado ya encajé bien. Me ayudó mucho tener a otras españolas en el equipo, que me ayudaron muchísimo, y ahora somos más", comenta entre risas Lucía, que comparte vestuario con Alexia Putellas, Mapi León, Jana Fernández, María Pérez, Daniela Arques y Elene Lete. "El fútbol en Inglaterra está a otro nivel, va muy rápido, y entrenar y competir al máximo nivel te aporta cosas muy positivas", comenta. "Este año tenemos un equipo con muy buenas jugadoras. Los fichajes se han adaptado rápido y bien. Creo que va a ser una gran temporada", finiquita quien tiene contrato hasta junio de 2030. En el Londres, Corrales luce su número preferido: el '7'. "Cuando llegué estaba libre, no me lo creía, así que lo cogí. ¿En la selección? Cuando me dejen...", reflexiona Lucía, que estudia Educación Social, pasea a su perrita en sus ratos libres y dice haberse adaptado sin problemas a Inglaterra.

articles.title: El Getafe necesita cargar las baterías
articles.standfirst: El equipo azulón tendrá que compatibilizar Liga y competición europea a la vuelta del parón de selecciones
articles.summary: El equipo azulón tendrá que compatibilizar Liga y competición europea a la vuelta del parón de selecciones
articles.body: El Getafe llega a este parón con la sensación de necesitar recargar pilas. Bordalás lo ha comentado ya en varias ocasiones y, de hecho, en la última señaló que este inicio de liga había sido un “sinvivir”. Con todo ello, los azulones se encuentran en mitad de tabla y lograron la clasificación a la Fase Liga de Conference League. El equipo getafense descansará durante este parón para volver con la batería al máximo ahora que arranca la competición de jueves y domingo con el inicio europeo. El equipo se ha hecho fuerte en casa, con tres victorias esta temporada, dos empates y ninguna derrota, aunque aún no sabe lo que es sumar lejos del Coliseum y eso está lastrando al equipo. El feudo getafense está sufriendo un lavado de cara que ha sorprendido a propios y extraños. El club dio un acelerón este verano y parece, como han dicho muchos, otro estadio. Y aún le falta más de un año para finalizar. El ‘Stamford Bridge Coliseum’ ha cautivado a una hinchada que sabe que falta techarlo, cerrarlo y finiquitar la fachada y la tribuna. El inicio de LaLiga para los azulones no podría entenderse sin su nuevo feudo. Los del sur de la Comunidad de Madrid tienen un ‘Tourmalet’ por delante, como apresuró a decir Bordalás en la última rueda de prensa. El cuadro azulón tiene un regreso del parón de selecciones cuanto menos jugoso, con visita al Spotify Camp Nou, viaje a Rumanía para verse las caras frente al Craiova en su debut de Conference League y recibir al Rayo Vallecano. Un verdadero regreso de ‘aúpa’ que vivirán los del Coliseum. El equipo da síntomas de cansancio, pero sigue compitiendo. Bordalás inculca que nadie puede rendirse y el gol de Azón frente al Málaga es buena muestra del ADN azulón. Eso, sumado a la clasificación actual, el pase a Conference y el estado del Coliseum ponen la nota positiva a este inicio de temporada. Fuera de casa el equipo no ha sumado. Cuatro salidas, cuatro derrotas. Lo pasó realmente mal en Serbia y a punto estuvo de quedarse fuera de la Fase Liga de Conference. En Mendizorroza, Sevilla y Pamplona el equipo tampoco sumó y es la gran asignatura pendiente. Esta primera fase de la temporada de los hombres de Bordalás se puede calificar con un 7. Ahora toca mantener el nivel para que el equipo pueda seguir en la parte media-alta de la tabla.. Enes Ünal se destapó como la gran alegría de la temporada. El turco, que quizá podía dejar dudas por sus dos operaciones de rodilla, en apenas minutos las solventó con su gol al Partizán y, más tarde, con el tanto al Racing que le dio los tres puntos. El otomano suma dos tantos siendo la gran alegría, seguido de cerca por otros nombres: No ha arrancado bien la temporada. Abqar llegó el curso pasado como uno de los grandes refuerzos en defensa y las lesiones no le dejaron mostrar el potencial que cautivó al Alavés. Este curso, los ruidos de fuera no han ayudado y ahora las lesiones lo vuelven a dejar fuera, habiendo jugado apenas dos partidos y habiendo visto la roja en uno de ellos.

articles.title: El milagro de Deco
articles.standfirst: El Barça ha configurado una plantilla profunda y de calidad sin grandes desembolsos
articles.summary: El Barça ha configurado una plantilla profunda y de calidad sin grandes desembolsos
articles.body: El Barça vive instalado en un momento de feliz casi permanente. Con una plantilla joven, una estrella como Lamine Yamal en pleno auge y un equipo que funciona casi a la perfección, las expectativas se han disparado. La mayor parte de los focos apuntan a Hansi Flick. El técnico alemán es el gran artífice del rendimiento excelso de un equipo al que solo le falta la Champions para confirmarse como uno de los equipos de moda. Pero el entrenador catalán no es el único culpable de este éxito. Deco, desde la dirección deportiva, ha conseguido dar una estabilidad económica al club, ajustar los salarios, dar profundidad a la plantilla y dotar a su técnico de infinidad de recursos en todas las posiciones del club. Y lo ha hecho desde la lógica, la mesura y la incorporación de futbolistas que, en muchos casos, no apuntaban a las quinielas de futuribles futbolistas del Barça. Fichar poco y bien ha sido la máxima del luso. Dos campeonatos de Liga, dos Supercopas de España y una Copa del Rey en tres temporadas, a la espera de lo que suceda en esta, son el preciado balance de un Deco que ha puesto orden en la tesorería del club. Y lo ha hecho sin devaluar a la plantilla, sino más bien todo lo contrario. La incorporación masiva de jugadores de la cantera ha permitido el director deportivo elegir minuciosamente los refuerzos necesarios, en muchos casos cuestionados, y lo visto sobre el terreno de juego, hasta la fecha, ha terminado por darle la razón. Las incorporaciones de Gordon y Adeyemi son los dos últimos claros ejemplos de ello. Además, Deco ha demostrado que no se casa con nadie y que ningún futbolista puede sentirse imprescindible en este Barça. Jugadores como Dembélé, Lewandowski o Ferran Torres han cerrado su etapa como barcelonistas y nadie se ha rasgado las vestiduras por ello. El mérito aumenta, además, si se compara con la trayectoria económica de las principales potencias europeas en esas cuatro temporadas con Deco al frente de las operaciones azulgrana. El balance entre fichajes y ventas del portugués le sale a devolver. Es decir, en positivo. 289,5 millones gastados para 20 incorporaciones por los 318 ingresados en las 31 ventas realizadas. 28 millones y medio de superávit. Por ponerlo en contexto en España, en esa misma franja de tiempo el Atlético presenta un balance de 175 millones en negativo y el Real Madrid de 408,5 millones. El que más se acerca al gasto moderado del Barça de Deco es el Bayern, que entre fichajes y ventas ofreció un balance negativo de 122,8 millones. Y, como casi siempre, las cifras se disparan si nos fijamos en la Premier. Los 569 millones del Arsenal, 618 del City o los 635 del Liverpool están a años luz del milagro en los despachos de Deco.

articles.title: Alarma en Francia por la situación y futuro de Mbappé en el Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: El diario 'L'Equipe' y Daniel Riolo (RMC Sport) muestran su preocupación por la situación que vive Mbappé en el Madrid y se muestran críticos con la actitud de Kylian
articles.summary: El diario 'L'Equipe' y Daniel Riolo (RMC Sport) muestran su preocupación por la situación que vive Mbappé en el Madrid y se muestran críticos con la actitud de Kylian
articles.body: En Francia se preguntan "por qué el descontento en torno a Mbappé en el Real Madrid no deja de crecer". El diario 'L'Equipe' considera que "la actitud de Kylian Mbappé, considerada demasiado individualista y poco discreta, sigue alimentando las críticas en Madrid. En el seno del club madrileño, la gestión de su comunicación genera cada vez más malestar". Antoine Simonneau subraya que el regreso de Mbappé a los entrenamientos con el Real Madrid un día antes de lo previsto no ha calmado el ambiente de desconfianza hacia Kylian: "Al contrario, las críticas y el descontento se han intensificado en los últimos días. La semana pasada, su salida a una discoteca en París y su posterior paseo en bicicleta por Suiza fueron percibidos por gran parte de la afición madridista y de los medios españoles como una falta de profesionalidad, dado que debía guardar reposo tras la lesión de rodilla sufrida con la selección francesa. El diario francés cree que el entorno madridista le reprocha a Mbappé que, a pesar de sumar 94 goles en 111 partidos no ha sumado ningún título como merengue, no mantener un perfil más bajo y anteponer sus intereses personales, como su candidatura al Balón de Oro, a los del club. "Tras más de dos años, da la impresión de que Mbappé todavía no ha entendido cómo funcionan el Real Madrid y su entorno, ni qué comportamiento debe adoptar... Está muy mal asesorado y, en términos de imagen, eso perjudica a todos: tanto a Kylian como al Real Madrid", le desvela una fuente interna del Madrid al diario 'L'Equipe'. Daniel Riolo, periodista en RMC Sport, comentó en 'After Foot' que el escándalo de la bicicleta de Mbappé es "una perla más del collar. He llegado a preguntarme: ¿sigue teniendo ganas Mbappé? ¿Qué es lo que quiere? Da la impresión de que se levanta cada mañana pensando: 'voy a pegarme un tiro en el pie'. No puede seguir acumulando errores de esta manera". "¿A cuántos internacionales hemos visto apoyando a su equipo? No digo que tenga que desplazarse a todos los partidos, pero en el Stade de France estaban todas las grandes leyendas, la familia del fútbol francés reunida. No digo que sea obligatorio, pero podría hacer algo en lugar de enviar ese mensaje que dice: 'me importa un bledo lo que penséis'. Pero llega un momento en que eso tiene un límite. Envía un mensaje positivo. Ven al Stade de France: 'no, no quiero'. Quédate en Madrid: 'no, no quiero'. No te dejes ver a la salida de una discoteca: 'no, no quiero'. Anda en bicicleta cuando Mourinho no quiere: 'no, no quiero'. ¡Basta! Te estás pasando, ¡basta!", comentó Riolo. Daniel Riolo también señala el "misterio en torno a la lesión de Mbappé" y observa un cambio en el estado anímico de Kylian. "Tengo la impresión de que mentalmente no está bien. Cuando lo dejamos tras el Mundial, todo iba bien. Estaba con sus amigos, disfrutaba, proyectaba una imagen fantástica. Luego, la obsesión por el Balón de Oro le lleva a esa forma de comunicarse... Ofendes a uno de tus amigos (Ousmane Dembélé); es una lástima hacerlo, pero lo haces. Hubo una explicación que, en realidad, no convenció. ¡Basta! Estás dándoles munición a tus detractores". En su opinión, Mbappé está enviando un "mensaje muy negativo": "Que no haya nadie en su entorno que se lo diga me lleva a la conclusión de que no está bien", insiste. "Su vida privada ha cambiado (mantiene una relación con la actriz Ester Expósito) y tiene derecho a estar enamorado, pero ¿acaso desea otra cosa? El fútbol le agota; todo lo que le rodea y las expectativas le cansan, justo en el momento en que cambia de patrocinador de forma sonada. No entiendo cómo se gestiona a sí mismo ni quiénes son las personas que le asesoran. No comprendo qué pretende hacer, ni esa actitud, ni ese distanciamiento de todos". "No descartemos una salida de Mbappé (del Real Madrid) al final de la temporada", vaticinó Daniel Riolo.

articles.title: Premier League football shirts made by workers on £1 an hour
articles.summary: A BBC Sport investigation traces official football shirt production to factories in Cambodia where workers are paid less than £1 an hour.
articles.body:
Workers are being paid a basic wage of less than £1 an hour to make official football shirts for some of the world's biggest clubs, BBC Sport can reveal.

Our investigation traced authentic replica shirts to two factories in Cambodia, where conditions were described as "grim".

We followed the supply chain behind official shirts after fans told us they were frustrated by rising prices, with many turning to cheaper counterfeits instead.

Images obtained from inside Bowker Garment Factory and Trax Apparel show kits being made for clubs including Arsenal , Celtic, Liverpool and Real Madrid.

Employees there told us they struggled to make ends meet and worked on up to 700 items a day as part of a production line.

In rare interviews, supported by documentary evidence and published anonymously, workers also described:

Safety concerns about electrical equipment.

The Clean Clothes Campaign , external - a global workers' rights network - said our findings painted a "very grim picture".

"These are issues that many garment workers around the world face every day," added spokesperson Emma Vogt.

Similar issues, such as low pay and high temperatures, have been reported across Cambodia's garment industry.

Research published last year suggested that, of a typical £85 shirt, £8.50 covers fabric, sewing and shipping, £37.45 goes to the retailer, £16.25 to the manufacturer, £9.50 on marketing and £13.60 in VAT.

Shirt prices have increased significantly over the past decade, though industry experts argue advances in technology and expensive kit deals with elite clubs have contributed to the rise.

Adidas does not own either factory, but both are primary suppliers subject to its workplace standards. , external

The sportswear giant supplies eight of the 20 Premier League teams.

Adidas said: "We have taken a variety of measures to ensure fair and safe working conditions for workers across our supply chain for more than 25 years.

"Through around 1,200 factory audits per year, we review and evaluate supplier conduct, work with suppliers to address issues and make improvements where necessary."

Six thousand miles from the club shops where these shirts will be sold, a meeting is taking place inside Bowker Garment Factory.

In a photograph obtained by BBC Sport, mannequins display Benfica, Aston Villa and Celtic kits beneath an Adidas logo on the wall.

About 3,400 people - most of them women - work here on the outskirts of Phnom Penh. Another 3,200 work 10 miles east at Trax Apparel.

Fabric is imported from Thailand and Vietnam before a specialist tailor makes a sample for other employees to follow.

Much of the shirt-making process then takes place at these factories, including sewing, ironing and packaging.

'These shirts contain the sweat of Cambodian workers'

Staff typically work six eight-hour shifts a week and, according to five payslips seen by the BBC, receive basic monthly salaries of $210-$220 (£158-£166).

The salaries comply with local minimum-wage laws, and three of the payslips indicate total monthly earnings of about $300 (£226) once overtime and allowances are included, albeit with significant extra hours worked.

"It's hard to live with this amount," said a Bowker worker, who explained she had little left after rent, food and utilities.

"I want international customers to hear that one shirt they buy costs more than two weeks' salary for a worker," said another worker at Trax.

"Every one of these shirts contains the sweat of Cambodian workers."

Trax told us its average monthly employee earnings range from $305-$342 (£230-£258) this year.

Adidas said average net wages across a sample of its Cambodian suppliers were 34% above the Anker Research Institute's living-wage benchmark, , external adding staff were "usually paid considerably higher than the local minimum wage".

Bowker did not respond to our request for comment.

'One shirt sells for $120. How much are they pulling in from 600 of them?'

In another photograph taken inside Bowker, a thermometer shows 35.2C and humidity of 57.6%.

"The heat stress is really taking a toll on our health," said an employee on the ironing line.

Workers at both factories described pressure to meet group production targets of between 300 and 700 items a day.

"Just think about that," they added. "If one shirt sells for $120 (£90) in the store, how much are they pulling in from 600 of them? They make a ton of money but give almost nothing to the workers."

Others described verbal abuse when targets were missed.

"When we can't complete the quota they scold and yell at us and tell us to resign," said a third worker at Bowker.

The same employee said they received two electric shocks from an exposed wire.

"I tried to report it multiple times, but they only took action after the second time I got shocked," they said.

Adidas told us both factories had "heat-management measures", that its standards "do not permit any form of harassment", and that "no electrical-related accidents" had been found in Bowker's records.

Trax acknowledged "periods of elevated temperature" but said cooling systems were in place and insisted its approach "is not based on enforcing output targets".

Such concerns are widespread across Cambodia's garment industry, with a 2024 International Labour Organization report , external finding 69% of factories had issues with heat and 84% with worker protection.

It's August Bank Holiday in England and two of the Premier League's top sides - Aston Villa and Arsenal - are about to meet.

Tens of thousands of people are at Villa Park - many wearing shirts made in Cambodia.

Arsenal 's latest home design was released in May, but we were sent photographs showing it inside Trax months earlier.

Fans of both clubs told us official shirts have become overpriced.

One Villa supporter has just paid £95 for his, complete with a Champions League badge.

"You buy your season ticket. Three shirts, that's around £300 on top. It's ridiculous," he said.

An Arsenal fan is struggling with the outlay for his whole family.

"I've got young kids now and I've started getting them kits, so it's started getting expensive," he said. "They're not cheap if you get the official ones."

Various studies estimate the global market for official football teamwear is worth several billion pounds.

"The mark-up on football jerseys... it's hard to imagine a more lucrative brand market," said Dave Welsh from The Solidarity Center , external - a US-based workers' rights organisation.

But former Puma and Umbro kit designer Rob Warner told BBC Sport last year that the economics behind shirt prices are more complex.

"A lot of the profit margin is made by the retailer because they're so dependent on the success of the team... it's a risk," he said.

"Then you factor in the cost of the kit deals going up, and the brands having to try to recover some of the money they're paying to the elite clubs."

Adidas supplies eight of the 20 Premier League clubs, plus Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

Fellow sportswear giant Nike supplies three, as well as England. Its football shirts have been produced in Thailand and Vietnam, and more recently Georgia.

Nike does not publish salary data by country, but told us 71% of its key suppliers pay at or above living-wage benchmarks relevant to their location.

Hummel, which also provides kit to three Premier League sides, did not respond to our enquiry.

'Respect has got to be a baseline in sport'

The average price of an adult replica Premier League shirt has risen by 50.7% over the past decade, helping fuel demand for counterfeits sold for as little as £12.

Many of those counterfeit shirts originate from China.

Fans have been warned against buying fakes, with police saying , external they can be "manufactured without regard for safety standards or workers' rights" and Trading Standards warning that "counterfeiters have no morals and no standards".

The Premier League expects clubs to carry out appropriate due diligence on their kit manufacturers and supply chains.

None of the clubs named in this article responded to our request for comment.

"Respect has got to be a baseline in sport," said Anna Bryher, from UK campaign group Labour Behind the Label. , external

"Clubs need to send a really strong message that they won't put their name on a shirt if workers are not treated with respect."

articles.title: Romano: ‘Conversations’ will ‘for sure’ take place — Man Utd on verge of agreement with ‘world-class’ defender
articles.summary: Manchester United are mulling over whether they should activate the 12-month option in Lisandro Martinez’s contract.Should they decide to do so, the centre-h...
articles.body:
Manchester United are mulling over whether they should activate the 12-month option in Lisandro Martinez's contract.

Should they decide to do so, the centre-half will be tied to Old Trafford until June 2028, rather than June 2027.

Given he has proven his 'world-class' abilities since joining the club in 2022, the only reason United would consider parting ways with Martinez is because of his checkered fitness record.

The World Cup winner is one of the side's most injury-prone players of recent years, having suffered at least one lengthy setback in each season he's represented United.

It means that now, after four years as a Red, he has accumulated only 80 Premier League appearances.

The most Martinez has made in a single campaign came in his maiden term, when he featured 27 times before fracturing his metatarsal, while his fewest came in the following season, when he played only 11 league games and for just 648 minutes across 2023/2024.

Yet, his stellar performances when he is fully fit may have done enough to buy him some time at United.

The 28-year-old is – by some distance – the best defender at Old Trafford, so Michael Carrick will be crossing his fingers that he stays available for the duration of 2026/2027.

Before Martinez enters what will be the final year of his deal, Fabrizio Romano has shared some insight into the situation: "Man United have a clause to extend the contract until 2028. So they feel calm. They feel in control.

"He's 28. So at the peak of his experience, he has had some bad luck with injuries over recent years, but Man United still believe in Lisandro as a leader – as a top defender.

"At the moment, the situation is under control. The conversations will take place, for sure, in the next few months. At the moment, this is not in advanced negotiations with any other side. So I would say that this one is considered under control."

articles.title: Declan Rice close to signing new long-term Arsenal contract
articles.summary: Declan Rice is close to signing a new long-term contract with Arsenal, per BBC Sport.The 27-year-old’s current deal expires in the summer of 2028, with the c...
articles.body:
Declan Rice is close to signing a new long-term contract with Arsenal, per BBC Sport .

The 27-year-old's current deal expires in the summer of 2028, with the club having an option to extend by another year.

Arsenal have been working to tie him down to a new deal. That process has now reached an advanced stage as both parties are close to a formal agreement.

Rice currently earns a salary of £240k per week, but the fresh terms will see that figure rise to around £350k per week.

This would put him on a par with the club's highest-paid player Bukayo Saka.

Rice has been nothing short of sensational since joining Arsenal from West Ham United in 2023.

The 27-year-old has been a consistent performer for the Gunners, impressing with his physicality, passing, ball-winning ability and attacking contributions.

He has bagged 21 goals and 33 assists in 165 appearances across all competitions.

The midfielder played a pivotal role in guiding Arsenal to their first Premier League title since 2004 last season.

Rice has earned 80 caps for the England national team. But he withdrew from Thomas Tuchel's squad for the recent Nations League games due to concerns over load management.

The former West Ham star is expected to be involved on Saturday when Arsenal host Leeds United at the Emirates Stadium .

The north Londoners will be eager to bounce back with a win after suffering a shock 3-0 loss at Brighton & Hove Albion in their last game.

articles.title: Santi Cañizares dicta sentencia sobre Mbappé y su 'caso bicicleta'

articles.body:
Santiago Cañizares , que fue jugador del Real Madrid en dos etapas (1988 a 1992 y 1994 a 1998), habló en el programa ' El Partidazo de COPE' sobre Kylian Mbappé y su polémico vídeo montando en bicicleta y su viaje a París.

"Me parece una chorrada... Es el último problema que tiene el Real Madrid", le dijo el exportero a Juanma Castaño .

articles.title: Mijatovic advierte a Mbappé sobre su vida privada: "Merece la pena tener más cuidado"
articles.standfirst: "Se podría haber llevado un poco mejor, pero también tiene derecho a disfrutar sus días libres. Hay que tener cuidado"
articles.summary: "Se podría haber llevado un poco mejor, pero también tiene derecho a disfrutar sus días libres. Hay que tener cuidado"
articles.body: Pedja Mijatovic, jugador del Real Madrid de 1996 a 1999 y director de fútbol de equipo blanco de 2006 a 2009, advirtió a Kylian Mbappé en el programa 'El Larguero' sobre sus actitudes fuera del campo de juego. "Nunca puedes saber qué ha pasado exactamente, si ha hablado con Zidane, si lo ha acordado con Mourinho... Hay muchas cosas que los jugadores pueden hablar con sus entrenadores y las desconocemos", le comentó el exfutbolista a Manu Carreño. Mijatovic cree que "en este momento todos los jugadores del Real Madrid tienen que tener mucho cuidado con las apariencias públicas, porque la gente está sensible, llevas dos años sin ganar un título y este año has empezado con muchas dudas. Tienes que estar pendiente de todo lo que transmites fuera de la Ciudad Deportiva"- "Eso se podría haber llevado mucho mejor en el caso de Mbappé. Hay que entender que es un chico joven y tiene que disfrutar sus días libres, pero merece la pena tener más cuidado", apuntó. Mijatovic también se pronunció sobre el polémico vídeo de Mbappé montando en bicicleta: "Tampoco lo entiendo, porque la bicicleta es una cosa normal, muchos futbolistas lo utilizan como preparación". "No creo que lo haya hecho adrede por las palabras de Mourinho, porque sé que tiene muy buena relación con él", apuntó. Pedja Mijatovic habló sobre la frialdad que transmite el Real Madrid de un Mourinho que parece que todavía no ha dado con la tecla táctica en el equipo. "El Real Madrid, en los partidos que he visto, ha transmitido más dudas que confianza. Mourinho todavía no ha encontrado esa energía que necesita para que el equipo arranque y vaya mejorando. Hay un ambiente un poco frío, es lo que transmiten. Todo lo contrario a otros equipos cuando los ves. Se puede poner como ejemplo a la selección española, que tiene un aire diferente y muy bonito de ver. Incluso cuando sufren, es bonito de ver. Y eso es lo que tiene que buscar transmitir el Real Madrid", analizó el de Podgorica.

articles.title: Real eye McTominay in Jan, Pio 100m 🤑 and Woltemade flop: morning news☀️
articles.summary: The wait is almost over: league football is back. After the international break, Serie A is ready to resume, and so are its big clubs. Today's papers are ful...
articles.body:
The wait is almost over: league football is back. After the international break, Serie A is ready to resume, and so are its big clubs. Today's papers are full of talking points, both on the pitch and... in the transfer market!

Let's take a look at this morning's top stories.

👎 Juventus, Woltemade already written off?

Nick Woltemade 's Juventus adventure has only just begun, but the German is already under scrutiny after his glaring miss for Germany . As La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, the forward born in 2002 has yet to fully convince in a Juventus shirt either: his tendency to drop deep and get involved in the build-up makes him more of a nine-and-a-half than an out-and-out striker, which is exactly what Spalletti 's team currently lacks. His straight loan from Newcastle, officially running until June 2027, also makes his future in Turin far from certain.

That is why Juventus have already started looking around ahead of next season. The players being monitored include Retegui, Balogun and Raimondo , while the winter window could offer opportunities to act immediately. Woltemade will still have time and opportunities to prove himself, but the centre-forward question remains unresolved in Turin: if the aim is to challenge at the top again, they will need to establish whether the German can really become the number nine who delivers goals and a constant presence in the opposition box.

💡 Milan, Amorim plans a new-look Diavolo

Ruben Amorim has always promised an aggressive Milan side that controls games, but maintaining balance has often meant making compromises so far. However, Saelemaekers ' injury could push the coach to be bolder against Sassuolo : as La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, a 4-2-3-1 with Chukwueze, Pulisic and Moreira behind Gonçalo Ramos , or Cisse replacing the Portuguese striker, is becoming an increasingly likely option. It would be the Rossoneri's most attacking setup, albeit with a few extra risks against a team dangerous on the counter.

The decision will also depend on the fitness of those returning from international duty and the recovery of Estupiñán and Bartesaghi , with the latter ready to step in if the Ecuadorian misses out. Modric should feature in midfield, while Jashari and Musah are competing for the other spot, with Rabiot a possible more cautious option on the left flank. Loftus-Cheek remains another alternative, but after the win over Lecce, Amorim seems determined to stick with the 4-2-3-1: the Sassuolo game could be the moment to see just how far Milan are willing to go on the attack.

His goals for Italy have sent Pio Esposito 's value soaring even higher, with the striker now considered one of the most exciting centre-forwards of his generation. As La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, the question is how much the player born in 2005 might be worth on today's market: Inter have no intention of selling him, but a figure of €100 million no longer seems so unrealistic. Comparisons with other youngsters signed for big money by Premier League clubs, from Hojlund to Sesko , support the idea of an ever-higher valuation for the Nerazzurri academy graduate.

Esposito's age, performances and potential for improvement are the main factors driving his value up. Roberto Mancini has already compared him to great centre-forwards of the past such as Vieri and Toni , while at Inter the young striker will need to keep carving out playing time alongside Lautaro and Thuram . After scoring 10 goals last season, the next step will be greater consistency, but the club have already decided to put their faith firmly in him: a long-term investment that underlines just how much the Nerazzurri believe in their gem.

⚠️ Napoli, does Mou want McTominay as early as January?

Scott McTominay 's future could hold a surprise. According to Il Mattino , Real Madrid have approached the Scottish midfielder's representatives, while Napoli continue working on an extension to his contract, which expires in 2028. If no agreement is reached, the situation could gather pace and lead to a possible sale as early as January .

However, the club do not appear willing to let their midfielder go easily, considering him central to Allegri 's plans. Besides Real Madrid, some Premier League clubs could also take advantage of the stalled contract talks to make a move. The final decision will rest with Napoli, who must choose whether to secure McTominay's future with a new deal or postpone any assessment until the summer.

Roma return from the break with two huge fixtures: Como and Real Madrid in just four days. As Forzaroma.it reports, Donyell Malen is ready to take centre stage again after recovering from his knee problem and returning to training with the squad. The Dutchman has already scored 6 goals in 5 games and is targeting the record of 36 league goals set by Higuain and Immobile . What's more, nobody in Serie A has scored more than him in 2026: 20 goals, compared with 13 each for Douvikas and Lautaro.

Dybala will play alongside him, while Pellegrini is the favourite ahead of Soulé and Rodrigo Mora for the third attacking spot. The Argentine, who only returned today along with Balerdi and Castro, could initially be rested ahead of the clash with Mourinho 's Real. In defence, meanwhile, Ndicka appears to be ahead of Balerdi. Roma are looking for a strong restart in Como to defend their lead at the top, with the home side's sporting director Ludi describing the fixture as "extremely difficult" and exciting.

💥 Lazio, Noslin is Gattuso's latest masterstroke

Lazio resume their campaign at the top of Serie A alongside Inter and Roma, with a team very different from the one seen at the start of the season. Much of the credit goes to Rino Gattuso , who has revitalised several players previously considered peripheral figures in just a few weeks. As Il Corriere dello Sport reports, the latest example is Tijjani Noslin , who scored two decisive goals in the last two games before the break and is set to start up front again against Monza . Pinamonti should start on the bench, although the pair could play together later in the game.

Noslin is merely the coach's latest successful gamble: before him, Mandas, Nuno Tavares and Belahyane all regained key roles and rediscovered their form. The Greek goalkeeper currently has Lazio's highest average match rating, while Tavares is their highest-rated outfield player after five rounds; Belahyane has also become a key figure in dictating play. The challenge now is to stay at the top: Gattuso is relying on a strong work ethic , discipline and a desire to improve to keep springing surprises.

🚀 Fiorentina, De Gea back to his best! His future...

Fiorentina are enjoying a David De Gea who is back to his very best. As Corriere dello Sport highlights, the Spanish goalkeeper has rediscovered his sharpness after a difficult season, proving decisive in recent outings against Venezia , Pisa and Napoli . At 36, the former Manchester United player continues to impress with his ability to bounce back and compete at the highest level. Now, as the league resumes against Genoa , he will also be looking to make amends for last year's performance at Marassi, when he saved a penalty from Colombo but also had some shaky moments.

His current form also reopens the discussion about his future . De Gea is under contract with Fiorentina until 2028 and relations with the club are excellent, but next summer could prove decisive: a departure was already considered a few months ago, partly because of wages amounting to around €3 million net per season . The desire to continue together prevailed, but the situation will be reassessed at the end of the season. Also waiting in the wings is Tommaso Martinelli , who came through Fiorentina's academy and is currently on loan at Avellino, tipped as a potential successor.

articles.title: La Fundación Atlético de Madrid celebra la gala de los I Premios ADN Rojiblanco
articles.standfirst: Enrique Cerezo, así como de Simeone, Koke, Johnny Cardoso, Alexander Sørloth, Lola Gallardo y Rosa Otermín, presentes en el acto
articles.summary: Enrique Cerezo, así como de Simeone, Koke, Johnny Cardoso, Alexander Sørloth, Lola Gallardo y Rosa Otermín, presentes en el acto
articles.body: Ayer tuvo lugar en el Club Telefónica del Riyadh Air Metropolitano la gala de los I Premios ADN Rojiblanco, una iniciativa nacida para reconocer y apoyar causas sociales que representan los valores que definen el sentimiento rojiblanco dentro y fuera del terreno de juego. Compromiso, solidaridad o entrega son algunas de las características presentes en los seis proyectos ganadores que fueron presentados por peñas del club, y que recibirán una dotación económica, reafirmando así el compromiso de la Fundación Atlético de Madrid con el uso del deporte y la educación como motores de transformación social. El evento fue presentado y conducido por las dos embajadoras de la fundación, Carla Pereyra y Beatriz Espejel. Enrique Cerezo, presidente y patrono de la Fundación Atlético de Madrid, dio la bienvenida al acto a los representantes de los proyectos galardonados y otros invitados, entre los que se encontraban Diego Pablo Simeone, Koke, Johnny Cardoso, Alexander Sørloth, Lola Gallardo y Rosa Otermín, integrantes de los equipos masculino y femenino respectivamente. También estuvo presente Adelardo Rodríguez, leyenda rojiblanca y presidente de la Fundación Atlético de Madrid. En el marco de los I Premios ADN Rojiblanco, un espacio para la solidaridad y el impacto social, el club quiso hacer entrega a la Fundación Aladina de una donación con el objetivo de ayudar a la construcción de 'Casa Aladina', el primer centro de día de apoyo integral para niños enfermos de cáncer, familias y supervivientes de cáncer infantil que habrá en Europa. Se ubicará en el distrito de Hortaleza, y permitirá que los niños y adolescentes enfermos de cáncer, sus familias y supervivientes puedan tener acceso a terapias y programas diseñados para mejorar su calidad de vida y bienestar emocional.

articles.title: Raul Asencio talks Ancelotti, injury and recent controversy: ‘I fully accept the consequences’
articles.summary: At a time when Real Madrid’s defensive crisis appeared unsolvable, Raul Asencio emerged from the academy and provided a reliable and solid solution to the fi...
articles.body:
At a time when Real Madrid's defensive crisis appeared unsolvable, Raul Asencio emerged from the academy and provided a reliable and solid solution to the first-team dynamics.

A few seasons have passed since then, but the player's importance has entered a downward spiral with little, if any, sign of encouragement.

Having already seen limited minutes in the last campaign, the player's prominence took a further hit this season with Jose Mourinho considering him to be saleable and not a part of his plans.

He eventually stayed, but has suddenly required surgery just when his chances were about to begin.

Asencio has undergone surgery. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Facing the microphone with Diario AS in a recent interview, the Real Madrid defender opened up on how the past year has been difficult for him, especially with injuries and the fissure he has been suffering from.

"It all started a year ago, and since January, the fissure had been holding up thanks to conservative treatment. The pain kept getting worse. "

"I was suffering, but I couldn't stop because the team came first. I always put this club and this badge above everything else," he added, speaking of his dedication.

Playing through the pain ultimately had its consequences, and they were very harsh on the player's continuity and place in the team.

"But there came a point when the fracture had grown, and I realized I had to undergo surgery."

The defender also opened up about Carlo Ancelotti with great words of praise for the current Selecao manager.

"Carlo Ancelotti? An excellent person. To me, he was much more than just a coach."

Asencio spoke highly of Ancelotti. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

"He was the person who took me under his wing, who believed in me, and who told me: 'You're staying with us,'" he added.

"I will always hold a special place for him in my memory," Asencio concluded on Ancelotti.

Earlier this year, the academy graduate came under immense scrutiny and criticism after he was convicted of drunk driving, especially given how he has been linked with negative charges and news even in the past.

Speaking on the same, Asencio said, "It was a very tough time. Several situations in my life converged within a short period."

"Mourinho wasn't wrong; he was absolutely right. Ultimately, people form opinions based on what comes out and what they see," he added, backing Mourinho's view on the incident.

The player then admitted publicly to having made a mistake and begged for forgiveness.

"I made a mistake. I admitted it then and I admit it now. I've apologised and will continue to do so."

"I'm a 23-year-old guy, and I've made mistakes, the kind anyone might make at that age. But I have to be aware of where I am," he added.

Asencio also acknowledged that playing for Real Madrid commands some basic requirements as a person, and that he would ensure not to cross lines in the future.

"I'm at Real Madrid, and this cannot happen again. I fully accept the consequences, and my only focus is turning this situation around."

"I'm the one who's hurting the most. I dream of turning things around and winning trophies with this club and this jersey, hopefully for the rest of my career. That's why situations like this won't happen again," he concluded.

articles.title: Women's World Cup 2027: How can England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland qualify?
articles.summary: England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland are among those hoping to qualify for next year's Women's World Cup. What awaits them in the play-offs?
articles.body:
England must get through two rounds of home and away ties to qualify for the Women's World Cup in Brazil.

Sarina Wiegman's European champions will play Greece in Crete in round one of the play-offs, with the first leg on Friday, 9 October at 17:30 BST.

The second leg will be played at home, at King Power Stadium in Leicester, on Tuesday, 13 October at 19:30 BST.

Commentary for both England matches will be on BBC Radio 5 Live.

Should England beat Greece over two games, they will face the winners of Slovakia v Ukraine, with the away fixture played first.

The exact dates of the potential second-leg fixtures are to be confirmed, although they will take place between 26 November and 5 December 2026.

England head coach Wiegman named her initial squad last month, with Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly notable absentees.

When asked why they were left out, Wiegman said: "They have not been playing to their full potential.

"Of course, I still believe in these players. They are really good and have shown so much for us."

Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live: "That is also why I didn't pick them this time, because they have not played to their potential in my opinion in the last couple of weeks.

"I had those conversations with them and that was very hard to take. They took it well and, of course, they want to work on that."

All you need to know about 2027 Women's World Cup

Northern Ireland, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland are also involved in the play-offs as they chase World Cup places.

As with England, they are in action on Friday.

In round one, Wales face Albania at 17:00 BST - with coverage on BBC Two Wales from 16:45 BST.

Scotland play the Czech Republic at 18:00 BST, available to watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC Alba.

Northern Ireland take on Portugal at 19:00 BST, available on BBC iPlayer.

Despite England securing five wins from their six qualifying matches, world champions Spain finished top of the Lionesses' group and secured the one automatic spot.

Wiegman said: "We knew what the play-offs would look like and, while we're pleased with the draw against Greece, the focus now is on making sure we're really well prepared.

"We want to dominate games and have a lot of the ball and that's something we will prepare for carefully."

Analysis: What are the home nations' chances?

England did not want to go through the play-offs but were given an unkind draw in the qualifying groups when they met world champions Spain.

However, Wiegman's side are in a strong position for the play-offs and will fancy their chances against Greece, who sit 55 places beneath them in the Fifa world rankings.

England also beat potential round two opponents Ukraine in both matches in the qualifying group stage, with an aggregate 9-1 score.

Northern Ireland face a tricky tie against a talented young squad from Portugal in round one. Portugal twice beat Northern Ireland in Euro 2025 qualifying.

Their task gets even harder if they make it through to round two, with potential opponents Iceland proving to be difficult to break down in their matches against England this year.

Scotland are hoping to reach just their second Women's World Cup finals, after a 2019 appearance. They failed to qualify in 2023 but have performed well this year, including drawing with Belgium, showing that they can compete with Europe's strongest teams.

They would need to produce their best in round two if they meet big-hitters Sweden, who have been semi-finalists in the past two Women's World Cups.

Wales have never beaten a top-20 ranked nation in a competitive fixture and are likely to need to do so to qualify.

There is optimism, though, as Rhian Wilkinson's side thrashed play-off opponents Albania 4-0 in their qualifying group.

Elsewhere, having performed superbly in qualifying, the Republic of Ireland have a tough play-off route with Belgium potentially waiting in round two.

First, Carla Ward's side will have to navigate a 3,100-mile trip to Kazakhstan, to tackle relatively unknown opposition.

articles.title: Liverpool academy: Working with Andoni Iraola and the future of the Reds' youth set-up
articles.summary: Liverpool academy director Alex Inglethorpe talks to BBC Sport about the value and future of Liverpool's academy.
articles.body:
One of the first things you notice in Alex Inglethorpe's office at Liverpool 's AXA Training Centre is a framed image gifted by Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It is a picture from 2019 of the academy director and player watching a game together. Alexander-Arnold left for a new challenge at Real Madrid last year, after 20 years on Merseyside, but his story is one of inspiration for everyone that enters Liverpool 's academy.

He joined as a six-year-old in 2004 and went on to win the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, League Cup, Community Shield, Uefa Super Cup and the Fifa Club World Cup with Liverpool .

"The ideal for any academy, and certainly for us, is wanting young players - and hopefully they're local players - to improve the first team and in doing so, they come and win trophies," says Inglethorpe.

"At Liverpool the bar is high, so to have a player capable of winning everything that you could possibly win is a dream."

Inglethorpe and his team oversee the development of younger players and ensure there is alignment between the academy and the first team.

One of the phrases used is 'the first team pitch is only 300 metres away from the academy building in Kirkby, but the journey might take 10 years to get there'.

Under new boss Andoni Iraola, players like Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and James McConnell, who have spent time at the academy, have all featured this season.

"We were fortunate because of how the calendar worked, with players still at the World Cup and a delayed return. Andoni and his staff spent a lot of his first week here watching the academy," says Inglethorpe.

"So we felt ahead, in terms of building a relationship from the outset."

At the Kirkby academy, phones are handed in on a morning and there is a clause in contracts with a maximum engine size limit for cars that are driven into academy premises.

"It comes back to passing your audition. First impressions matter," says Inglethorpe.

"Often before you've kicked a ball, the car you drive or the watch you wear can have an impact on how you're thought of - and that could be first team staff or players looking at you.

"We've believed in the idea of 'earning the right' for some time."

Last week, Manchester United signed 16-year-old winger Isaac Konde from Liverpool on a one-year scholarship followed by a five-year professional deal. Both clubs are now in talks over a compensation package.

In February, a tribunal ruled Liverpool must pay at least £2.8m to Chelsea for Ngumoha. The 18-year-old left Chelsea in September 2024 to join the Reds and signed his first professional contract a year later.

Both are recent examples of the current climate around talent.

At Liverpool , the belief is they have been sensible and responsible with a view to deferred gratification in most cases, but the wage structure is currently under review.

"It's always a compliment when other clubs want your players as it means you're doing something right," says Inglethorpe.

"But I think the market of players at 16 is distorted because of Brexit and because you can't recruit like you would do before. There's always been movement of players but it feels a little more extreme now.

"When there's a clamour for talent - fees, wages and everything else will shift accordingly, so it's dealing with what we have and adapting to a new situation."

Do Liverpool need a Scouser in the first team?

When Curtis Jones moved to Inter Milan in the summer, it left Liverpool without a first team player born in the city.

"I acknowledge the fact that ideally Liverpool would love to have a team full of Scousers," says Inglethorpe.

"But it is testament to the supporters that if you adopt the characteristics of a Scouser - and you only have to see the likes of Bill Shankly, Kenny Dalglish and others over the years - you can be treated as one of their own.

"So if you are fearless, passionate, play tough and demonstrate those qualities, then it doesn't matter if you've come from an L1 postcode and got a purple bin or not. That's the beauty of the club and the crowd."

One name to keep an eye on is 15-year-old Luca Eden. The midfielder was born in the Wirral and has already represented England at youth level.

Last month, he became the youngest player to feature in the Uefa Youth League for Liverpool , beating a record previously held by Joshua Abe, Ngumoha and Alexander-Arnold.

"We've got plenty of Scousers in the academy and plenty who I think will play for the club. But if not and a lad comes from Warrington or wherever, that's not a problem," Inglethorpe insists.

One of the most challenging aspects of Inglethorpe's role is letting players go. Liverpool released eight players from their academy set-up at the end of last season.

Inglethorpe explains how the likes of Harry Kane, who was coming through the academy at Spurs when he was a youth coach there, and Alexander-Arnold weren't necessarily the best in their respective youth cohorts.

"At that stage, there's too many unknowns. You can't predict how players will react to adversity and natural bumps in the road," says Inglethorpe.

"I've been proven wrong so many times in the past. A good example would be Jarell [Quansah] - someone who was always liked and never in danger of leaving but probably never seen in the top three in the group."

Quansah left Liverpool for Bayer Leverkusen in 2025 and has since won eight caps for England.

"There are no certainties - the point of the academy is to allow them to fulfil their potential," says Inglethorpe.

"Sometimes players need to leave to gain an opportunity. There are lots of lovely examples of boys leaving and having good careers, and I'm not convinced they would have had the same career if they stayed at Liverpool .

"The linear and most productive way is to break in, but there's different pathways that can lead back to playing for Liverpool - and that is the dream."

Just before the academy players go on the pitch, there is a sign that says: "Don't look sideways" - referring to where the first team train.

Next month will mark 14 years at Liverpool for Inglethorpe. So what's his definition of success?

"Anyone would want to take something on and leave it in a better place, and I think we've done that," he says. "Ultimately we have had players in the first team winning major trophies and we're fortunate to be part of that era."

The 'Kids Cup', when Liverpool beat Chelsea in the 2024 Carabao Cup final. Faced with an injury crisis, Jurgen Klopp relied heavily on academy players and his side finished the match with a team whose average age was under 22. Klopp called it his "most special trophy".

"It's definitely a moment in time. The longer the game went on, Jurgen was taking off the seniors and putting another one of the boys on. It was an incredible show of belief," says Inglethorpe.

On another wall in Inglethorpe's office is a magnetic board with headshots of every player in the academy on the left and the first team squad on the right. Ultimately, the motive is for everyone to make the journey across the board.

With a £20m revamp to the academy facility planned to be completed by 2028, the determination to carry on producing first team players is stronger than ever.

"There are exciting times ahead with the potential for the other end, and I'm really excited for the future," says Inglethorpe.

"In Julian Ward [the new sporting director], we have someone who is hugely invested in the academy and has been on this journey for a long time."

articles.title: Jorge Vilda deja de ser seleccionador, pero Marruecos lo mantiene en su estructura
articles.standfirst: La Federación marroquí lo anunció en un comunicado, sin dar más detalles
articles.summary: La Federación Marroquí lo anunció en un comunicado en el que informó sobre una concentración de las 'Leonas del Atlas' bajo las órdenes de Eric Blahic, el nuevo entrenador
articles.body: El técnico francés Eric Blahic fue nombrado nuevo seleccionador del equipo femenino de Marruecos, en sustitución del español Jorge Vilda, que deja ese cargo tras dirigir la selección marroquí durante tres años. Sin embargo, la noticia, según pudo saber MARCA, puede tener trasfondo positivo. La decisión de relevar a Vilda se conoció este miércoles a través de un comunicado de la Federación Marroquí de Fútbol (FRMF) que informó sobre una concentración de las 'Leonas del Atlas' en Rabat bajo las órdenes del nuevo entrenador francés. La Federación marroquí, sin embargo, no especifica (por ahora) los planes de futuro que tiene para el técnico que dirigió a la Roja al título Mundial en 2023 en Australia y Nueva Zelanda. En la última Copa de África de Naciones, disputada el pasado julio en el país magrebí, la selección marroquí -subcampeona en las dos últimas ediciones- quedó en cuarta posición tras caer en semifinales frente a Camerún (en penaltis), pero consiguió clasificarse para el Mundial Femenino de Brasil 2027. ¿Por qué tiene muchas 'chances' Vilda de seguir en la estructura de la Federación? Marruecos valora esta clasificación (segunda en su historia) para un Mundial de fútbol femenina; valora el estilo ofensiva del equipo y el 70% de triunfos conseguidos por Vilda; valora esa final de la Copa África conseguida dos años antes de esta última; pero, más allá de los resultados, valora la mejora en el nivel de muchas de las jugadoras marroquíes que hoy día están en algunas de las mejores Ligas del mundo (el ejemplo es Sakira Ouzraoui, del Madrid Cff). El legado de Vilda es indudable en estructura interna y desarrollo de las jugadoras. Por eso, la Federación marroquí lo mantiene por el momento a Vilda en su estructura, aunque no saben detalles de dónde.

articles.title: Robbie Ure, la cuenta pendiente del ataque del Sevilla
articles.standfirst: El escocés es el único delantero que todavía no ha visto puerta en lo que va de curso
articles.summary: El escocés es el único delantero que todavía no ha visto puerta en lo que va de curso
articles.body: Robbie Ure vuelve a estar disponible para Luis García Plaza. El delantero escocés ha regresado de su periplo internacional sin ver puerta, prolongando la sequía que le acompaña desde que viste de blanquirrojo. De hecho, es el único delantero de la plantilla del Sevilla que todavía no ha marcado en las siete primeras jornadas del curso. Ha participado en todas ellas, acumulando 397 minutos, y suma una asistencia, frente al Atlético de Madrid. Este próximo lunes tendrá una nueva oportunidad para reencontrarse con el gol frente al Levante. Hace dos meses, el Sevilla alcanzó un acuerdo con el Sirius para que Robbie Ure se convirtiese en el '9' del Sevilla durante las próximas cinco temporadas. El delantero escocés, de 22 años, estaba firmando una campaña sobresaliente en Suecia, donde acumulaba 20 goles en 20 partidos. Desde entonces ha incrementado su valor de mercado en dos millones de euros -de cinco a siete-. El jugador ha tenido que adaptarse a la liga española.... y al clima. "Creo que esta liga es mucho más táctica. Por supuesto, los defensores son mejores. Creo que en la liga sueca hay más goles y en LaLiga no hay demasiados goles en cada partido. Así que creo que esas son las dos mayores diferencias y quiero seguir adaptándome a esto y estoy seguro de que lo haré", dijo recientemente en una entrevista a El Correo de Andalucía. Lucas Stassin jugó 36 minutos en su debut frente al Espanyol y marcó. El belga se está recuperando de su lesión y aunque todavía no trabaja con el grupo, no se descarta su presencia en la lista para el partido frente al Levante. Isaac Romero, por su parte, firmó un gol y una asistencia frente al Athletic. Ure ha aportado muchas cosas al Sevilla aunque todavía no haya visto puerta. El escocés se estrenó provocando un penalti en el descuento del partido frente al Rayo Vallecano que dio a los de Nervión sus primeros tres puntos de la temporada. Su presión en San Mamés fue clave en la expulsión de Yuri y también en la acción sobre Unai Simón que terminó propiciando el tanto de Oso. Robbie Ure llegó a Nervión con el objetivo de aportar gol y convertirse en una referencia ofensiva. Un '9' de 1,89 metros, potente y con movilidad, capaz de fijar a los centrales, asociarse lejos del área y atacar los espacios. En Suecia ya demostró su capacidad goleadora; ahora busca trasladar ese instinto al Sevilla.

articles.title: La BMV se queda con una sola pieza
articles.standfirst: Bellingham se ha convertido en la pieza más fiable de la BMV y en el punto de partida para la mejoría del Madrid de Mourinho
articles.summary: Bellingham se ha convertido en la pieza más fiable de la BMV y en el punto de partida para la mejoría del Madrid de Mourinho
articles.body: Jude Bellingham ha vuelto a encontrarse. Mientras Mbappé convive de nuevo con molestias en su rodilla y Vinicius todavía busca su mejor momento físico y futbolístico, el inglés se ha convertido en la pieza más estable de la BMV. El tridente sigue siendo la gran esperanza del Madrid de Mourinho, pero es Jude quien está ofreciendo ahora mismo mayor continuidad. No se trata de señalar a sus dos compañeros. La temporada acaba de empezar y ambos tendrán mucho que decir. Pero en un equipo que todavía está buscando su mejor funcionamiento, Bellingham ya está respondiendo. Y lo hace en Madrid y con Inglaterra. O al menos así lo reflejan los números. El centrocampista suma tres goles y dos asistencias en ocho partidos oficiales con el Real Madrid. Pero la producción de Jude no acaba ahí: 91% de acierto en el pase, 52 recuperaciones, 52 duelos ganados de 84 y hasta 12 pases clave en este arranque de temporada. Una de las claves de su recuperación está en la posición que le ha dado José Mourinho. El técnico portugués está utilizando a Bellingham como mediapunta en su 4-2-3-1, más cerca de la portería y con libertad para aparecer entre líneas. La apuesta busca recuperar una de las principales virtudes que mostró el inglés en su primera temporada en Madrid: su capacidad para llegar al área y decidir. En aquella campaña, Bellingham marcó 23 goles y repartió 13 asistencias, unos registros que le llevaron a terminar tercero en el Balón de Oro. Después llegaron más responsabilidades en el centro del campo, problemas físicos y una temporada en la que su influencia ofensiva disminuyó. Ahora Mourinho parece haber encontrado una fórmula para devolverle parte de aquella libertad. Bellingham continúa teniendo trabajo defensivo y peso en la construcción, pero su posición de partida es más adelantada. Desde ahí puede aprovechar mejor su llegada, su conducción y su capacidad para aparecer en el área. Con Inglaterra, la fórmula es diferente pero la idea se parece. Thomas Tuchel está tratando de sacar partido de la versatilidad de Bellingham y ha llegado a probarle como delantero centro. El cuerpo técnico inglés quiere además un equipo más fluido, con libertad para que sus jugadores intercambien posiciones. La respuesta llegó ante Croacia. Bellingham participó en cuatro de los siete goles de Inglaterra: marcó uno y asistió en otros tres. Una exhibición que ha disparado todavía más los elogios en su país. Roy Keane fue uno de los más contundentes. El exfutbolista destacó la calidad del jugador con balón, pero puso especialmente el foco en su trabajo sin él y en la capacidad que tiene para contagiar al resto. "Puede llegar a convertirse en uno de los mejores de todos los tiempos", aseguró a ITV. El comentario refleja hasta dónde ha llegado la consideración de Bellingham en Inglaterra. Ya no se habla sólo de una estrella joven del Real Madrid, sino de uno de los líderes de una selección que quiere construir su futuro alrededor de él. Y en Madrid, la sensación no es muy diferente.
