articles.title: Is Jeremiah Smith the Best College Football Wide Receiver Ever?
articles.summary: Each and every week, regardless of the opposition, Jeremiah Smith does something absurd. And it all looks completely normal.
articles.body:
Each and every week, regardless of the opposition, Jeremiah Smith does something absurd. And it all looks completely normal.

This isn't exactly a new revelation. Ohio State's star wide receiver has been producing jaw-dropping moments since his very first game as a true freshman.

Years later, and we're struggling to quantify what it all means and how the staggering production stacks up. Forget about comparing him to other wide receivers and players currently playing each and every Satur

day. With all due respect, it's not close.

He's the best player in the sport, and there isn't much debate at this point.

Instead, we find ourselves drifting toward nostalgia and something more historic. More specifically, we're already comparing Smith, whose legacy is still very much unfolding, to the best wide receivers to ever grace a college football sideline.

How close is he to being the best wideout college football has ever seen? Let's explore.

Presently, Smith is the favorite to win the Heisman, and it feels like it will require a gargantuan effort to dethrone him from his post.

Sure, that seems like a hasty thing to declare in early October, although we've rarely seen a start to the college football season quite like this.

In five games, Smith has amassed 823 yards receiving and nine touchdowns. He's also averaging a ridiculous 18.7 yards per catch.

He torched Texas. He torched Iowa. The only team he didn't exactly torch was Kent State, and that's because he barely played once it quickly became a blowout.

At 6'4" and 225 pounds, Smith is an athletic anomaly. Despite his size, he's still one of the fastest players on the football field. It makes him an impossible cover, and it's been that way for years.

The No. 1 recruit in the country, Smith was an instant star. As a freshman, he scored 16 touchdowns. He also helped lift Ohio State to a national championship.

As a sophomore, he scored 13 times. Each time he found the endzone, his reputation grew.

Smith's 3,381 receiving yards currently rank eighth all time in the Big Ten. He's currently 407 yards away from the No. 1 spot, which he should obliterate if he stays healthy.

Again, he's just a junior. And we're not yet in the middle of October.

Physically and statistically, he is a unicorn. The position has seen its fair share of unique athletes, but this is something different.

He has the build, the hands, the stats and the hardware.

He won the Heisman, which is an appropriate place to begin.

Only four players to play wide receiver have won that award, and DeVonta Smith's triumph in 2020 was the first time a wideout had won in nearly two decades.

That alone puts the Alabama star in rarified air, and he earned it. In 13 games that season, he totaled 117 catches for 1,856 yards. He added 24 touchdowns. And in the College Football Playoff, taking on Notre Dame and Ohio State, Smith scored six touchdowns in two games.

Oh, and Alabama won the national championship.

In terms of individual seasons, given everything that was accomplished, it's hard to find any blemishes. And while many of these players possess an incredible frame, Smith dominated opposing defenses despite weighing roughly 170 pounds and at six feet tall.

Smith caught 235 passes for 3,965 and scored 47 touchdowns in his decorated Alabama career, which was one of the most productive in SEC history. The fact that he won a Heisman and a national championship lifts his resume in a special place.

Fitzgerald's college football journey began at Valley Forge Military Academy, largely because his academic situation demanded him to do so.

A year later, the Pitt freshman caught 69 passes for 1,005 yards and 12 touchdowns. But this was just the start.

Fitzgerald's sophomore year is widely regarded as one of the best the position has ever seen: 92 catches, 1,672 yards and 22 touchdowns.

Oh, and he set a record by catching a touchdown in 18 consecutive games, which is a feat that is hard to wrap your head around. At the time, it seemed like an impossible stretch to maintain, but he did just that.

In 2003, Fitzgerald's season earned him a runner-up finish in the Heisman. And at 6'3" and nearly 220 pounds, the wideout had the size and athleticism to do anything on the football field. It's this frame that made him so coveted by NFL scouts, which translated to becoming the No. 3 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.

Expert CFB Predictions for the Biggest Week 6 Games 🔒

No player has ever made the position look easier or cooler; this much we know for certain. And if you were to ask the many defensive backs he ran past and jumped over, they would likely provide an expected answer.

Before Randy Moss began terrorizing NFL defensive backs, he was Chad Pennington's favorite target at Marshall.

Before getting to Marshall, Moss was committed to Notre Dame. Then he decommitted and wound up at Florida State. Off-the-field issues ultimately resulted in Moss's dismissal, prompting to land at Marshall.

Over the next two seasons, Moss evolved into one of the greatest deep threats the sport has ever seen, catching 174 passes for 3,529 receiving yards.

Even more staggering, however, is his 54 touchdown catches.

His 1997 season earned him a fourth-place finish in the Heisman, finishing behind Ryan Leaf, Peyton Manning and Charles Woodson.

Moss used his 6'4" frame to regularly leap over opposing defensive backs, and he had the speed to run past any defender. His incredible NFL career certainly plays a role in the general assessment of the player, which is remarkable.

One thing is abundantly clear. He's in a genre of his own creation.

If we're simply looking at the numbers, Julio Jones probably doesn't belong in this conversation. Let's address that from the start/

In his three-year career at Alabama, Jones finished with 15 touchdown receptions. In his best (and final) season in 2010, Jones caught 78 passes for 1,133 yards and seven touchdowns.

Compared to others, he falls well short on the box score side.

But to simply define Jones' success as college wide receiver to his overall numbers would do him a great injustice.

For starters, no player meant more to Nick Saban and Alabama's dynasty than Jones. His commitment alone sent shockwaves through the recruiting world, and his imposing presence and rare physical gifts made him an enormous piece of Alabama's plans.

Jones was 6'3" and 220 pounds when he played in Tuscaloosa. In many respects, no player over the past 15 years had a body type and playing style to Jeremiah Smith than Jones, who could also do it all.

The only difference is Alabama's offense required him to do less. To the surprise of no one, he was also a superb blocker.

This one is more difficult to quantify. Jones helped Saban win his first national championship in Tuscaloosa, the start of a movement that changed college football.

If he played for a different school or in a different system, things would have been different.

One of the few players larger than Jeremiah Smith, Calvin Johnson spent his college football career at Georgia Tech, playing in run-heavy systems that struggled to throw the ball.

Despite that, he was a two-time All-American with the Yellow Jackets, the 2006 Biletnikoff Award winner and still managed a 15-touchdown season. He finished his career with nearly 3,000 yards receiving and 28 receiving touchdowns.

But again, stats aren't the argument. Johnson was a human highlight machine.

At 6'5" and 239 pounds, Johnson ran the 40-yard dash in an eye-popping 4.35 seconds. While this isn't a story dedicated to the best NFL Combine performances of all time, this showcased the kind of athlete he was.

On the football field, few players have ever been more unguardable. If that were the criteria, it would be hard to justify picking anyone else.

Michael Crabtree played two seasons at Texas Tech. He won the Biletnikoff Award in both of those seasons.

As a redshirt freshman, Crabtree racked up 134 catches, 1,962 receiving yards and 22 touchdowns. Playing in Mike Leach's Air Raid offense certainly helped. As did catching passes from Graham Harrell, who was the perfect QB for Leach's pass-heavy system.

But Crabtree was more than just a system player. He was on the receiving end of a Harrell touchdown pass that upset unbeaten Texas in November of 2008 with only a second left—a result that felt larger than life in the moment.

To this day, it remains one of the most iconic plays in CFB history.

In his two seasons, Crabtree totaled 231 catches, 3,127 yards and 41 scores. He produced these numbers despite being only 6'1" and not possessing overpowering speed.

When it comes to video game numbers and iconic moments, this is your guy.

The list of talented wide receivers is far too long to mention just a select few. Here are a few others worthy of consideration.

Desmond Howard, Michigan: He won the Heisman in 1991, and he was capable of flipping a game with hands, feet and on special teams. Howard's unique list of contributions made him a truly unique threat.

Tim Brown, Notre Dame: Speaking of Heisman winners, enter Tim Brown. The winner in 1987, Brown was a dynamic player for the Irish on offense and as a returner.

Justin Blackmon, Oklahoma State: With 253 catches, 3,564 yards and 40 touchdowns, Blackmon was a two-time Biletnikoff Award winner. He also finished in the top five for Heisman voting twice.

Jerry Rice, Mississippi Valley State: Sure, he played at a smaller school, but he was (unsurprisingly) wildly productive. Before he dominated in the NFL, Rice caught 27 touchdown passes in one season.

The only certainty surrounding Jeremiah Smith's future is that this will be his final collegiate football season. That decision has yet to be officially announced, of course, but it has never been easier to connect these dots.

Statistically speaking, Smith is operating at a pace few players have ever approached, even if he forgoes one year of eligibility entirely. And if it continues throughout this season, with massive games against Indiana, USC, Oregon and rival Michigan still to come, we could be looking at one of the greatest seasons the sport has ever seen.

If he ultimately wins a Heisman, and he'll be a difficult player to unseat, it will only elevate his accomplishments. Adding another national championship to his resume would only beef up his case further, and the possibility of doing so is very real.

Indeed, the position has seen its fair share of great players. Plenty have earned the right to be considered the greatest to ever play the position for a variety of reasons. Accomplishments are celebrated differently depending on who you ask, and there will never be consensus on such a heavy proclamation.

But Smith is clearly in the discussion. This much we know.

It's his physical gifts. It's the moments he produces. It's the numbers he accumulates. It's his impact on every game and play. Ohio State has grown accustomed to producing star wide receivers, although it's never had one like this.

In time, we'll have a clearer picture of what it all means and where Smith truly sits among the all-time greats. But thankfully, we have just that.

articles.title: SPFL pays out close to £50m in record year
articles.summary: The Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) pays clubs a record £49.6m in the past year.
articles.body:
The Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) has paid clubs a record £49.6m in the past year.

The league body has increased distributions by £7.6m, an 18% rise, with the bulk of money coming from broadcasting deals, licensing, match data and sponsorship.

"In an increasingly competitive international rights market, these results are testament to the enduring attraction of the SPFL," said chief executive Neil Doncaster.

"These are by far the strongest financial results in the SPFL's history, with turnover and total group distributions both surpassing the records set last year, and we are determined to maintain that momentum."

Scottish Premiership crowds topped four million for the first time last season as the league continues to attract the highest per capita attendances in Europe.

Figures published by Uefa showed approximately six million Scottish supporters watched men's matches during the 2025-26 campaign, with 900,000 in the lower leagues, 200,000 at domestic cup ties and 800,000 at European matches.

"Successfully balancing broadcast revenue with match-day attendances and the unique atmosphere created within packed stadia is central to the SPFL being recognised widely as one of the most intense, compelling, and emotive sporting competitions in the world," added Doncaster.

articles.title: Man City guilty charges: Everything Pep Guardiola said about case while manager
articles.summary: BBC Sport examines Pep Guardiola's comments about the Manchester City financial rule-breaking case during his time managing the club.
articles.body:
"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

Comforting words of solidarity from a long-standing leader can be a great source of strength and unity at a time of crisis.

And many Manchester City fans will have felt just that after former manager Pep Guardiola posted on social media last week in response to the club being found guilty of deliberate financial rule-breaking over nine years.

To some, Guardiola's intervention came as a surprise. After all, he is no longer in a managerial position having left City in the summer, and so was under no obligation to comment.

In the past, Guardiola - who joined City in 2016, most of the way through the 2009-18 period the charges relate to - had insisted guilty verdicts would change his relationship with the club.

He was outspoken on some matters during his time in Manchester, including Catalan independence and Israel's military offensive in Gaza.

But in some instances he sidestepped questions on human rights in the United Arab Emirates, whose government includes key members of City's hierarchy, and didn't broach the UAE's alleged role in the ongoing conflict in Sudan, which has accused it of being complicit in genocide. The UAE has strongly rejected the allegations.

City are, of course, appealing against the guilty verdicts, and Guardiola remains employed by owners City Football Group as a global ambassador.

Next week he is expected to attend City's Champions League tie against Paris St-Germain - the club's first home match since the guilty verdicts were announced.

But what did he say about the Premier League's case against the club over the years?

BBC Sport has taken a look at every significant comment Guardiola made on the subject during his time in charge at Etihad Stadium.

Senior figures worried about Man City being in next season's Champions League

Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City

"Do you know the question you're asking me?

"Did I receive money for another situation, right now, today? Honestly, do you think I deserve to have this type of question, the day we won the treble... did I receive money? Are you accusing me of receiving money?

"I listen to my chairman and my CEO, and I trust them. They tell me we are fair and we absolutely follow the rules. I believe them."

Guardiola's first comments on allegations of financial rule-breaking by Manchester City were delivered furiously, at a media conference in the immediate aftermath of a 6-0 victory over Watford in the FA Cup final.

He had been asked by Sky News' Rob Harris whether he had ever received separate, undeclared payments from the club in addition to his contracted salary, after the Football Leaks website published hacked information suggesting former manager Roberto Mancini had been paid in such a way.

Guardiola appeared to take the questions as an attack on his personal integrity.

Mancini said last month: "It's not an issue that concerns me. It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

" Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

19 February 2020 - bullish over Uefa appeal

"We appeal. When someone believes they are right, they have to fight. The club has to fight and I trust the club 100% what they have done and they have explained to me.

"This situation is not finished and we will wait. But until it is resolved you have to play and play, and that is what is going to happen."

Guardiola was responding after Uefa found City guilty of breaking its Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules, and banned the club from European competition for two years.

He was bullish regarding the club's right to appeal.

14 July 2020 - Champions League suspension overturned

"We were damaged. The people say we cheated and were lying - and many times. The presumption of innocence wasn't there."

The Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) had lifted the Uefa suspension and cleared the club of the more serious charges, finding some were unproven or that in some cases too much time had passed since the alleged rule-breaking.

Guardiola suggested in response that the wider football world had simply assumed the club was guilty and fair treatment had been lacking.

"Why did I defend the club and the people? It's because I work with them.

"When they are accused of something, I ask them: 'Tell me about that.' They explain and I believe them.

"I said to them: 'If you lie to me, the day after I am not here. I will be out and I will not be your friend any more. I put my faith in you because I believe you 100% from day one and I defend the club because of that.'"

Guardiola made clear he had built a level of trust with those in the City hierarchy that meant he inherently believed them.

But he also insisted he would resign if the club were found guilty, and distance himself from anyone who had 'lied' to him.

Guardiola had, of course, left the club in the months before the guilty verdict was confirmed last week. But in response he reaffirmed his kinship with City and chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

Manchester City and the 115 Charges Explained

10 February 2023 - first response to 115 charges

"My first thought is that we are already being condemned. I am fully convinced we will be innocent.

"Personally, I am happy we are here. We have the chance to defend [ourselves]. I think we have good lawyers. I think the Premier League, supported by 19 teams, will have good lawyers too.

"Just in case we are not innocent we will accept what the judge in the Premier League decides, but what happens if in the same situation that Uefa happened we are innocent - what happens to restore or pay back our damage?"

In an extraordinarily tense media conference after the Premier League announced it was pursuing 115 charges against City, Guardiola again insisted the club were innocent and suggested confidence their legal team would secure a result in their favour.

The Spaniard again suggested the media and public were predetermining City's guilt without a fair hearing.

"We would love [the verdict] tomorrow - this afternoon better than tomorrow.

"What we won on the pitch, we don't have any doubts."

A few months into a process that would take just over three and a half years, Guardiola expressed exasperation with the amount of time the Premier League investigation was taking and the doubt being placed on his team's achievements by pundits, the media and fans.

24 November 2023 - staying to manage in League One

"You are questioning like we have been punished. And in the moment, we are innocent until guilt is proved.

"I know the people want it. I know, I feel it. I will wait. Wait and see it and after the sentence has been done we will come here and explain it.

"There is more chance [for me] to stay if we are in League One than if we were in the Champions League."

Guardiola made two key pledges here - a media conference in response to the verdict when it was eventually revealed, and to continue managing the club in the lower leagues if such a punishment was handed down.

His summer exit thwarted the latter, but he would repeat the media conference promise later.

23 August 2024 - final weeks before hearing

"I am happy that it starts soon and hopefully it will finish soon. We will accept [the verdict], like we have always done."

In the months before the legal hearing into the charges began, Guardiola again expressed a desire for haste.

13 September & 21 September 2024 - hearing begins

"I know what people are looking for. I know what they are expecting - I know it because I have read it for many years.

"Everyone is innocent until guilt is proven. It's like everyone doesn't expect us to be not just relegated, they want us to disappear off the face of the earth."

Guardiola again insisted the football world was against City from the outset, as the legal hearing into the case began.

7 February 2025 - anticipating a final verdict

"In one month, I think there will be a verdict and sentence."

Briefings at the time indicated a verdict was expected in early 2025. Guardiola was under the same impression, but in reality it was a long way off.

The independent commission panel expressed its frustration with the time taken when it eventually published its findings last week.

"I trust them. I spoke with them and trust how they behave and how they did. What happened, happened.

"If you find me, yeah, but that will be difficult."

On leaving City, Guardiola underlined his belief in the club's innocence for a final time and his belief that individuals in the club's hierarchy were telling the truth.

In the final line, Guardiola again insisted he would give a media conference once the verdict was given - if journalists could find him.

No such media conference has been announced. The only subsequent comment Guardiola has made was last week's social media post.

The post featured photos of him holding trophies and posing with key City ownership figures including Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano - the men under pressure - but no players.

What the verdict means for his legacy is something football fans around the world will determine for themselves.

articles.title: Max Dowman, el Messi inglés de 16 años, ya tiene tres récords en el Libro Guinness
articles.standfirst: El futbolista del Arsenal es el Jugador más joven en la UEFA Champions League, el Goleador más joven en la Premier League inglesa y el Futbolista más joven en ganar la Premier League
articles.summary: El futbolista del Arsenal es el Jugador más joven en la UEFA Champions League, el Goleador más joven en la Premier League inglesa y el Futbolista más joven en ganar la Premier League
articles.body: Max Dowman, el niño prodigo de Mikel Arteta en el Arsenal, ha recibido tres certificados oficiales del Libro Guinness de los Récords (Guinness World Records) tras su meteórico ascenso en el fútbol inglés y europeo. El mediapunta de 16 años es el 'Jugador más joven en la UEFA Champions League: 15 años y 308 días', 'Goleador más joven en la Premier League inglesa: 16 años y 73 días' y 'Futbolista más joven en ganar la Premier League: 16 años y 144 días'. Max Dowman aparece en la edición de 2027 del libro 'Guinness World Records Football Edition' como parte de la "Promoción del 27". Max Dowman se entrena con el primer equipo del Arsenal desde los 14 años. John Terry, quien conoció a Dowman gracias a su labor como entrenador en la academia del Chelsea, está impresionado con el joven centrocampista. El mito del Chelsea no dudó en comparar las habilidades de Max Dowman con las de Leo Messi. "Lo vi jugar contra el Chelsea hace un año, y no he visto a nadie regatear como lo hace este hombre, excepto a Messi", compartió el mítico central en TikTok. Terry no dudó en justificar la comparación de Dowman con Messi: "Es una comparación muy grande, pero este chico es un talento de verdad. Va a ser una parte importante del futuro del Arsenal y también de Inglaterra". El conocido periodista Henry Winter compartió sobre Max Dowman que "evidente que es especial. Por ahora es potencial, pero es un potencial que pronto se convertirá en realidad", y lo comparó con Kaká. "Hay un pequeño elemento de Kaká en la forma en que toma la pelota y avanza con elegancia. Parece engañosamente rápido y atraviesa el campo con facilidad", explicó.

articles.title: Premier League talking points: Man City in spotlight with trip to Liverpool, Man Utd and Spurs desperate for win and Viktor Gyokeres' Arsenal chance
articles.summary: The Sky Sports Football writers analyse every game as the Premier League returns after the international break; Man City head to Liverpool while Arsenal host Leeds; Watch five games live on Sky Sports this weekend, including Man Utd vs Tottenham and Liverpool vs Man City
articles.body:
Can Gyokeres step up and save his stalling Arsenal career?

Arsenal vs Leeds - Saturday, 12.30pm kick-off

For the first five Premier League games of the season, Mikel Arteta named the same Arsenal front four in every single one. But now he's set to be forced into changes.

Hamstring injuries to Kai Havertz and Christos Tzolis mean the centre-forward and left-wing positions are likely to change over the next few weeks, at the very least.

Arsenal's squad strength allows Eberechi Eze to come in as a left-wing option. It's not a bad option. But how will Viktor Gyokeres fare as he prepares to replace Havertz?

It's been a frustrating start to the season for the Swedish forward, who has yet to score in his five appearances in all competitions so far this term. He's started only two, and he's managed just one shot in his 192 minutes so far.

Right now, Gyokeres is increasingly becoming the player who just doesn't quite fit at Arsenal. The start of the season has not only proved that Havertz is the clear first-choice No 9, but the German is better suited to Arteta's Arsenal system.

But there are signs Gyokeres could get his opportunity at the right time. First, he has a strong record against Leeds, scoring three goals in the two Premier League games against the Whites last season.

He also had a promising international break, scoring in every Sweden match during the lengthy camp. It mirrors a similar situation Gyokeres had in March of this year.

With question marks over his goalscoring form at Arsenal, Gyokeres went away with Sweden and fired them to the World Cup with four goals in two games. That in turn sparked a run of five goals in eight matches for Arsenal - with those goals helping the Gunners to the Premier League title.

Gyokeres' Arsenal career is currently stalling, can he kick it into gear? Sam Blitz

Bees to strengthen European dream or Villa's rebuild to continue?

Aston Villa vs Brentford - Saturday, 3pm kick-off

Aston Villa ended on a high by beating Tottenham before the international break, but a familiar and in-form foe now stands in their way.

Brentford beat Unai Emery's side three times last season. Twice in the league with two narrow 1-0 victories, and they also knocked them out of the Carabao Cup with a penalty shoot-out win.

The Bees have gone from strength to strength since and sit in fourth place with nine points from their opening five games thanks to their unbeaten start in the top flight.

An impressive 3-0 win against Chelsea marked their last outing and it will be a big ask for Villa to build on the victory at Spurs with a win here.

The rebuild at Villa Park - both in the squad and within the stadium itself due to the renovation of the North Stand - is taking shape. But Villa are not the polished product they once were.

Brentford will be full of confidence and victory on the road will be viewed as another building block towards their dream of European football.

For Villa, it could be another step in the right direction for their new era, or a stark reminder that a rebuild of this magnitude will require patience of the highest degree to recapture their usual consistency. Patrick Rowe

Palmer back in spotlight as Chelsea seek response

Chelsea vs Bournemouth - Saturday, 3pm kick-off

Cole Palmer had looked to be returning to his best. There were six goal involvements in seven games before the international break. "That's why we nominated him," said a rather disgruntled Thomas Tuchel when he was quizzed about Palmer pulling out of the England squad.

The England boss - who has been able to play Palmer just three times during his time in charge - said Chelsea informed him the forward "plays with discomfort and pain". Pointedly, Tuchel added: "He misses too many opportunities" to impress for England.

Xabi Alonso will need Palmer back available and ready to make an impact this Saturday at Stamford Bridge, though. Top-scorer Joao Pedro is set to be out again and Chelsea are badly in need of a response to the 3-0 loss at Brentford last time out, which knocked an encouraging start to the season off course.

Palmer's pal and Chelsea team-mate Morgan Rogers had a productive time away with the national team - capping that spell with a wonderful assist for Harry Kane on Tuesday night. It would be timely for Palmer to deliver a special moment of his own to get Chelsea back on track and shake off those negative headlines with a reminder of his quality. Peter Smith

Ipswich to stake survival claim or Fulham to dust off cobwebs?

Ipswich vs Fulham - Saturday, 3pm kick-off

Must-win? Six-pointer? Is it too early for this type of talk? Undoubtedly - but there are reasons to suggest otherwise.

Fulham sit 19th in the table with just two points from their opening five games. Ipswich know how difficult it is to keep their place in the Premier League.

Alvaro Arbeloa's side face all three newly promoted teams in their next three games and a win to kickstart that run would alleviate some of the early pressure they are finding themselves in.

Meanwhile, Ipswich will know Manchester City are on the horizon after this fixture and three points could take them into the top half of the table to build on their solid return to the top flight so far.

The game will not be decisive come May, but they could look back on this fixture as the game Fulham dusted off the cobwebs or where Ipswich staked their survival claim. Patrick Rowe

Can Brighton pick up where they left off?

Sunderland vs Brighton - Saturday, 3pm kick-off

No club likes an international break, but Brighton might have been particularly peeved at the timing. Five games in, they sit in third and are the Premier League's top scorers (16).

Brighton have lost just once in all competitions, and even that was a narrow 4-3 victory against Chelsea - something they would be confident of winning if they played again now.

And two and a half weeks ago, they swept aside champions Arsenal with a convincing 3-0 win at the Amex - but will the Seagulls' wings have been clipped by the extended break?

Casual fans might hope not - Brighton have been a delight to watch so far this season - but Sunderland will certainly hope they can take advantage of some post-break rustiness.

The Black Cats have arguably not amassed the points they deserve based on performances so far. Despite losing 5-3 to Man City before the international break, a few minor swings either way could well have seen Sunderland come away with the points that day.

But Brighton will come to the Stadium of Light full of confidence, hoping the momentum remains with them. Charlotte Marsh

'Lads, it's Tottenham'… but it's not that simple

Manchester United vs Tottenham - Saturday, kick-off 5.30pm, live on Sky Sports

On paper, the famous words are staring Manchester United fans in the face: "Lads, it's Tottenham."

Bottom of the table, winless after five games and already looking short of confidence… what could possibly go wrong?

Spurs have endured a miserable start under Roberto De Zerbi, but United arrive with their own problems. Just two wins from seven games in all competitions has piled the pressure on Michael Carrick, while three consecutive Premier League games without victory mean another slip-up will only turn up the heat.

History does favour United: they have won 40 of the 68 Premier League meetings, while Spurs have lost 25 times at Old Trafford.

But with both managers desperate for a result, this is less "Lads, it's Tottenham" and more "Lads, it's time to deliver."

Given it's at Old Trafford and the fact Spurs could match United's points tally with a win a defeat would feel marginally more disastrous for Carrick's side. William Bitibiri

Will Palace give old boss Glasner late gift on Selhurst Park return?

Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest - Sunday, 2pm kick-off, live on Sky Sports

Oliver Glasner left Selhurst Park a hero at the end of May when his side lifted the Conference League trophy, their first ever European silverware, in his final game in charge.

He returns barely four months later hoping his old side will be in generous mood as he looks to build some consistency following what has been an odd set of results in his first five league games in charge of Nottingham Forest.

Draws with Liverpool and Spurs were decent results and it looked like things had begun to settle with victory at Aston Villa, but the scoreline from, and the nature of, the 1-0 reverse at home to previously winless Coventry last time out will have stung.

Palace themselves are still adjusting to the post-Glasner era under Pierre Sage, and defeat at home to Ipswich last time out was particularly dispiriting.

They will be as aware as anyone of underestimating their old boss, who won only one of his first seven games in charge of the Eagles before winning six of his next seven and never looking back. His former employers will just have to hope this isn't the weekend that things click this time around. Ron Walker

Hull City vs Everton - Sunday, 2pm, live on Sky Sports

The international break may have come following Hull's first Premier League defeat of the season, but that sentence alone is enough for fans to be overjoyed. Up until matchday five they had earned their place inside the top four with a remarkable start.

They return to action in eighth, which is still a major overachievement even at this stage. One place above them, is Everton.

The Toffees have been quietly going about their business and remain unbeaten. Given the question marks over their squad following the summer transfer window, it's yet another mightily impressive start spearheaded by David Moyes.

It makes for an intriguing return to league action for both sides, who will no doubt be riding a wave of positivity. The visitors though have a chance to teach the hosts a real lesson.

Last season, Everton were the seventh-best team in the Premier League on away turf. This term, they have picked up points on their travels to Bournemouth and Tottenham. If there's one thing they know how to do, it is keep home fans quiet.

That will be easier said than done at the MKM Stadium given the buoyant atmosphere one would expect. However, if Everton can produce a trademark on-the-road performance, it could be a sobering experience for Hull and a dose of reality that there is still a long way to go before you can celebrate anything. Callum Bishop

Can Liverpool produce statement win to kick-start Iraola reign?

Liverpool vs Man City - Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm, live on Sky Sports

Anfield would be red hot any time Man City came to visit, but after recent events, expect a particularly volatile atmosphere on Sunday for a clash that could act as a springboard for Andoni Irola's Liverpool reign.

While the Basque is still unbeaten and could become only the third permanent Liverpool manager to avoid defeat in each of his first six top-flight matches in charge of the club this weekend, he has enjoyed a favourable run of fixtures to begin his tenure.

That all changes now though, with the Reds face a tough-looking trip to Brentford, before hosting in-form Brighton & Hove Albion and champions Arsenal following the City encounter, an exacting league run that will tell us much more about how well Iraola's ideas are taking hold.

The Liverpool head coach does have injury worries to key personnel to contend with, but if he can overcome those to produce a statement win in front of the watching world on Super Sunday , then players and fans will really start to believe in the new man. Rich Morgan

How will City's perfect start be affected by Premier League verdict?

Anfield is famous for its atmosphere, but the mood awaiting Manchester City on Sunday will be unique. What a venue for City's first game since an independent commission judged they broke Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018. Seismic.

City are appealing, of course, but the Liverpool crowd will deliver their own verdict and expect it to be vociferous. On the pitch, for what that is worth, Enzo Maresca's City side are defending a perfect record of five wins from five and are currently top of the table.

Andoni Iraola is also unbeaten since taking over at Liverpool but with three draws from their opening five games, this feels like the first big test of his reign - and his team's own title credentials. Whatever happens, all eyes will be on an Anfield clash to remember. Adam Bate

First PL win in 25 years secured… now Coventry aim for home victory

Coventry vs Newcastle - Monday, 8pm, live on Sky Sports

The international break arguably came at the worst possible time for Coventry. Frank Lampard's side earned a vital 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest, their first top-flight win in 25 years. However, a three-week break denied Coventry of the chance to build momentum following a poor start to the season.

Home matches have been miserable so far this campaign. They've lost all three in all competitions, with an aggregate score of 9-1, including two goalless defeats in the league.

Only five teams in Premier League history have lost each of their opening three home matches of a campaign without scoring, a record they'll be desperate not to join.

Newcastle's the name that arguably excites Lampard the most when checking the fixture list. The former midfielder won 16 times against this weekend's opposition as a player, and only Crystal Palace have been defeated more times (5) than Newcastle (3) with Lampard in the opposition dugout.

Coventry, however, have not had much success against Newcastle. The hosts have lost seven out of their last eight encounters, including five in a row.

But with Newcastle's last away league game ending in a thumping loss to Leeds, and Coventry tasting a Premier League win for the first time since 2001, could Monday bring their first home top-flight win in 25 years? Luca Adewale

articles.title: Women's World Cup play-offs: Ella Toone called up by England as Lucy Bronze withdraws
articles.summary: Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone receives a late England call-up for this month's World Cup play-off games against Greece.
articles.body:
Ella Toone has received a late call into the England squad for this month's Women's World Cup play-off ties against Greece.

Manchester United midfielder Toone, and Arsenal winger Chloe Kelly, were omitted from the initial squad with manager Sarina Wiegman saying "they have not played to their potential in my opinion in the last couple of weeks".

Toone has scored 24 goals in 69 senior England appearances, winning Euro 2022 and Euro 2025 as well as starting in England's 2023 World Cup final defeat by Spain.

Toone said after being left out of the squad: "It's been a really difficult week. It's not the news that any footballer wants."

Meanwhile, Chelsea defender Lucy Bronze has left the squad and will return to her club to manage a minor injury sustained in league action last weekend against West Ham.

The Lionesses arrived in Crete on Wednesday evening to prepare for Friday's first leg against Greece at the Pankritio Stadium in Heraklion.

The second leg takes place at Leicester City's King Power Stadium on Tuesday, 13 October.

The winners face either Slovakia or Ukraine on 26 November and 5 December in a two-legged play-off to decide which team progresses to next year's Women's World Cup, which is being held in Brazil from 24 June to 25 July.

articles.title: Mazazo para el Sporting: Antonio Casas, fuera hasta 2027
articles.standfirst: El delantero andaluz tendrá que frenar durante los próximos meses tras la lesión sufrida ante el Celta Fortuna
articles.summary: El delantero andaluz tendrá que frenar durante los próximos meses tras la lesión sufrida ante el Celta Fortuna
articles.body: Otro golpe más para el Sporting. Si no era suficiente con la casi decena de bajas con las que contó el conjunto rojiblanco la pasada jornada, la lesión de Antonio Casas es más grave de lo que se esperaba y tendrá que frenar durante los próximos meses de competición. Un nuevo contratiempo para los gijoneses, que perderán hasta el nuevo año al que estaba siendo su pichichi durante el inicio de temporada. Salvo sorpresa, Antonio Casas no jugará hasta 2027. El delantero andaluz sufre una lesión de grado 3 en el bíceps femoral derecho que le apartará de los terrenos de juego entre dos y cuatro meses. El futbolista cedido por el Venezia sufrió una rotura en la victoria ante el Celta Fortuna por la que fue sustituido al descanso. Tras el encuentro, Casas se sometió a las primeras pruebas médicas. La inflamación de la zona obligó a que se realizase un nuevo reconocimiento ayer, cuando se concretó la gravedad de la lesión. Un mazazo justo después de su explosión en Gijón. Tras un par de jornadas de toma de contacto, el ex del Córdoba se estrenó como goleador en la visita al Andorra. Dos semanas después, el día de su lesión, Casas anotó su primer doblete como rojiblanco, convirtiéndose en el pichichi del Sporting y en el jugador con un mejor promedio de gol por minuto de la categoría. Una alegría que apenas le duró unos instantes. Una lesión que echa más leña al fuego en Mareo. El entrenador Nicolás Larcamón, el presidente ejecutivo José Riestra y más personal del club mantuvieron una reunión de urgencia en El Molinón, tras la victoria ante el Celta Fortuna, para identificar las posibles causas de la plaga de lesiones de las últimas semanas. Si bien el argentino recuperará a varias de las bajas de cara a la próxima jornada, el Sporting sufre un nuevo mazazo con la grave lesión de Antonio Casas.

articles.title: Afcon 2025 final verdict: When will Cas crown Morocco or Senegal champions?
articles.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport is set to rule on the decision to strip Senegal of their Afcon 2025 title. But fans should not expect an immediate verdict.
articles.body:
Everyone knows a football match should take 90 minutes but, in its own way, the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) has been playing out for nearly nine months.

Now, finally, one team or the other - either Morocco or Senegal - willl grab the winner. Only that moment of glory will come in a courtroom, not on the pitch.

On Thursday, Sport's highest legal authority - the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) - will hear Senegal's appeal against the decision to strip them of the title they thought they had won back in January against the hosts in Rabat .

But those hungry for a resolution have already been warned it will not arrive on the same day.

So how did we get here? And what happens next?

In front of 66,000 home fans creating an electric atmosphere inside Rabat's Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium, Morocco appeared set for a date with destiny as they chased their first Afcon title since 1976.

Instead, the final descended into chaos deep into stoppage time.

With the match still goalless, Senegal thought Ismaila Sarr had scored a dramatic winner, only to discover that referee Jean Jacques Ndala had already blown for a Moroccan free-kick.

The controversy deepened in the 98th minute when, after a VAR review, Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty.

Tempers boiled over on the touchline and in the stands. Senegal coach Pape Thiaw led some of his players and staff down the tunnel, while supporters clashed with security as order briefly collapsed.

Play eventually resumed and, in the 124th minute, Morocco missed a golden chance to end their 50-year wait for continental glory when Real Madrid's Brahim Diaz failed to convert a penalty, chipping it 'Panenka' style into the grateful arms of goalkeeper Edouard Mendy.

Pape Gueye's extra-time strike then secured a 1-0 win for Senegal, who lifted the trophy for a second time.

'Shameful' and 'terrible look' - the chaos that marred Senegal's triumph

Senegal decries imprisonment of fans after Afcon clashes

Why was the Afcon final result overturned?

Unsurprisingly the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FMRF) quickly lodged a complaint with the Confederation of African Football (Caf), arguing Senegal had breached competition regulations.

Article 82, contained within a chapter titled "Withdrawals", states: "If, for any reason whatsoever, a team… leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee" they shall be "considered the loser and shall be eliminated from the current competition".

In March, a Caf appeals board agreed, ruling that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory .

While there is precedent for Caf overturning results during Afcon and World Cup qualifying, others, including one former senior Caf official, argued that only the referee has the authority to abandon a match if a walk-off occurs.

The FMRF said it was seeking the proper application of tournament regulations, but Senegal's federation (FSF) described the ruling as "unfair, unprecedented and unacceptable" and appealed to Cas.

Afcon final 'deficiencies' dealt with - Motsepe

Denounce 'abject' Afcon decision - senior Caf member

What is the Court of Arbitration for Sport?

Founded in 1984 and based in the Swiss city of Lausanne, Cas was set up as an independent legal body designed to settle disputes as global sport became more lucrative and, as a result, more litigious.

For governing bodies which recognise Cas' authority, it is deemed to be the supreme arbiter, meaning its ruling is final unless, in rare cases, Switzerland's highest court decides to set it aside based on a limited number of technicalities.

More than 900 cases are filed every year, from more than 50 different sports, covering issues such as employment contracts and transfers, doping, corruption, TV rights and, in this case, the organisation of sporting events.

The appeal will be heard by a panel of three arbitrators chosen by Cas for their expertise in sports law.

In this instance, the panel will be led by 76-year-old Frenchman Gerald Simon, founder of the Sports Law Laboratory at the University of Burgundy and a Cas member for 23 years.

If the panel fails to come to a consensus, its president will make the final decision.

How does Cas work and why can't Man City appeal to it?

While the hearing, which will be heard in private at the request of the parties involved, is expected to end on Thursday afternoon, Cas have already warned that this is merely the starting point of the panel's deliberation.

In a statement, the court warned it "cannot state when a final decision will be rendered but it will not be on the day of the hearing".

Having already waited nearly nine months to get to this stage, the bad news is that the Cas code states that appeal verdicts should be delivered a maximum of four months after a hearing, though guidelines also say panels should aim for less than three months.

The good news is that it can be quicker.

In 2020, Manchester City appealed to Cas over Uefa's decision to ban them from European club competitions for breaching financial fair play regulations.

The hearing took place on 8 June with the verdict landing in City's favour on 13 July.

Even though Caf's appeals board is independent, a reversal of its judgement would deliver another blow to the reputation of African football's governing body, which has already been heavily criticised for the retrospective decision to hand Morocco the title.

Caf president Patrice Motsepe said back in March that they will "adhere to" and "respect" whatever Cas decides, so if things go in Senegal's favour, it could mean someone having to tinker with the Afcon rulebook.

The Teranga Lions' walk-off has, however, already brought about a change in football's rules.

"The referee may sanction with a red card any player who leaves the field of play in protest at ⁠a ​referee's decision," said Ifab, the game's lawmaking body, back in April.

"This new rule will also apply ​to any team official who incites players to leave the field of play. A team that causes a match ​to be abandoned will, in principle, forfeit the match."

Thiaw has already been given his marching orders by Senegal, having lost his job following the team's last-32 World Cup exit , while Walid Regragui, the man in the Moroccan dugout back in January, was dismissed in March .

Both men will no doubt still view success with Cas as a moral victory.

Whatever the outcome, animosity is likely to linger between the two federations.

The FMRF's senior hierarchy were furious with Senegal's behaviour, believing the pictures beamed around the world irrevocably tarnished the image of the first Afcon hosted by the kingdom since 1988 - a tournament into which a huge amount of time and money had been invested.

The FSF and the Senegalese government have, meanwhile, leaned into a feeling prevalent across the continent that Morocco holds too much influence within African football .

Other incidents also irked them, such as laser pens being directed into players' eyes and ball boys moving goalkeeper Mendy's towel, something which eventually led to the barely believable sight of reserve keeper Yehvann Diouf being tackled to the ground by three ball boys when he tried to intervene.

With the next Afcon scheduled to take place in June and July next year, the chances of a high-profile rematch between Africa's best two teams is a tantalising thought.

But while the chaos of this year's final may have given birth to a new rivalry for fans to revel in, there is unanimous agreement that such encounters should be settled on the pitch and not in a courtroom.

articles.title: ¿Queda empañado el legado de Guardiola en el Manchester City?
articles.standfirst: El City afronta las consecuencias de las infracciones financieras mientras el legado de Pep está en el centro del debate tras diez años de dominio absoluto en Inglaterra
articles.summary: El City afronta las consecuencias de las infracciones financieras mientras el legado de Pep está en el centro del debate tras diez años de dominio absoluto en Inglaterra
articles.body: Durante una década, Pep Guardiola convirtió al Manchester City en una de las grandes referencias del fútbol mundial. Su llegada en 2016 marcó el inicio de una etapa histórica en el Etihad, pero el reciente veredicto de culpabilidad del club por graves infracciones de las normas financieras nos deja una pregunta, ¿hasta qué punto puede afectar este caso a su legado? Guardiola solo estuvo al frente del City durante las dos últimas temporadas del periodo investigado, y el club ya ha anunciado que recurrirá el veredicto. Aun así, durante su mandato llegaron algunos de los futbolistas (Bernardo Silva, Gündoğan, Walker...) que están bajo sospecha y que terminarían construyendo una de las plantillas más dominantes del fútbol inglés. De ahí que separar completamente los éxitos deportivos del contexto institucional resulte complicado. Los números del entrenador catalán, sin embargo, hablan por sí solos. Pep llevó al City a conquistar 100 puntos en la Premier League 2017-18, consiguió el primer triplete nacional de la historia del fútbol inglés y se convirtió en el primer entrenador en ganar el triplete continental con dos equipos diferentes. Además, consiguió algo que nadie había logrado antes en la máxima categoría inglesa: cuatro títulos de liga consecutivos. “Cuando ganas 20 títulos, es por eso que llevas 10 años ahí. Como entrenador, tienes que ganar, si no te despiden”, explicaba el propio Guardiola. Su impacto trasciende incluso los trofeos. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, presidente del City, considera que Guardiola no solo transformó al equipo, sino que “cambió la Premier League”. Una percepción compartida por entrenadores como Daniel Farke y Thomas Tuchel, que lo sitúan entre los técnicos más influyentes de la historia. “Es simplemente el mejor”, llegó a decir el actual entrenador del Leeds. Pero el debate sobre su legado queda inevitablemente condicionado por el contexto institucional del club. Rodri, uno de los grandes protagonistas de esa etapa, insistió: “lo que hicimos, no nos lo pueden quitar”. Zabaleta, ex jugador del City, puso en valor la etapa de Pep: “No estoy seguro de que el club pueda ganar absolutamente todo en los próximos 10 años" después de lo conseguido por Guardiola. El veredicto puede manchar la imagen institucional del Manchester City. La discusión más compleja es hasta qué punto debe hacerlo con Guardiola. Sus títulos, sus récords y su influencia en el fútbol inglés siguen siendo parte de una década extraordinaria. La duda que queda abierta es si, con el paso del tiempo, ese legado será recordado por su fútbol o inevitablemente bajo la sombra de las irregularidades del club.

articles.title: Ronald Araujo has been Liverpool's most important summer signing so far by balancing Andoni Iraola’s side from right-back
articles.summary: Ronald Araujo is just a loan signing but the summer arrival from Barcelona has already helped steady Liverpool's season under Andoni Iraola. With insight from Araujo's former team-mate, Adam Bate examines why Araujo has made such a swift impact at Anfield…
articles.body:
It is understandable that the arrival of a 27-year-old defender on loan from Barcelona has not brought the same buzz as the £123m man Bradley Barcola. Nor does Araujo engender the same excitement about his potential that has greeted Jeremy Jacquet.

But there are signs already that his acquisition late in the summer transfer window could prove significant for Liverpool. Araujo is helping to solve a problem position. A centre-back by preference, the Uruguayan has brought balance in the right-back role.

Jeremie Frimpong left Liverpool too open in those first two games of the season. He was removed after Nottingham Forest took the lead midway through the second half at Anfield and has not been seen in Andoni Iraola's Premier League starting line-up since.

Araujo does not merely mirror the work of Milos Kerkez on the opposite flank. He gives Liverpool the option of building in a three and has the instincts to sweep across. His presence makes Iraola's team less vulnerable to the switch of play and from set pieces.

Indeed, Araujo has won 15 aerial duels since the Ipswich game - more than twice as many as any other Liverpool player during that time. Look at his defensive action areas so far this season and it is clear that he is contributing inside his own penalty box.

Within the club, he has impressed with the speed of his adjustment. Speak to those close to him and they suggest that Araujo has been struck by the step up in standards even compared to Barcelona but that he is relishing it, invigorated by the opportunity.

That should be no surprise because this is a player who always thought about the game and been willing to embrace the challenge. Diego Scotti was a senior colleague when Araujo broke through as a teenager at Boston River and has stayed in touch ever since.

"From the first day, he caught my attention," Scotti tells Sky Sports . "I was struck by his personality, his dedication, and the intensity with which he trained. I saw him taking the game very seriously. He was a youngster very interested in learning and in listening.

"Every day, I saw him train with a lot of dedication, which is important in this profession. That was the first thing that surprised me about him. And, as well as his talent, more than anything else, I was surprised by his physical characteristics at such an early age.

"He soon joined the team and it was as if he had been competing for many teams in the top division. Obviously, there were errors. His positioning, when to play and when not to. But they were errors that he quickly corrected. Technically, he improved day by day."

Scotti anticipated his rise. "I had no doubt that he was destined for elite football. He was playing for Uruguay at 20." But going to Barcelona accelerated that development. "At Barcelona, he polished everything. His technique, his control, his passing."

He adds: "When you can combine that with a strong aerial game, his physical qualities, his personality and his attitude… Something that I always liked about him was that he was humble. He would listen to what older players told him. He was always receptive.

"Even now, he is always willing to collaborate. I am personally in charge of the Footballers' Union in Uruguay. He is very attentive to what is going on in our country. He does not forget where he came from. I think that is remarkable. He is a good teammate."

As well as helping Liverpool to tighten up defensively, Araujo has shown that he can make an impact at the other end of the pitch too. Most notably, there was his clever flick that opened up the chance for Dominik Szoboszlai to level it up against Atletico Madrid.

That was an outlier but Araujo has shown himself to be capable in that supporting role. Certainly, he gives Liverpool more defensively than they lose offensively. "Sometimes, because he is a centre-back, we underrate his offensive side," said Iraola that evening.

"He gave a great assist for Dominik Szoboszlai, he made a couple of very good surges from his position. I am very happy with him. He has come with a willingness to show he belongs to this level and I hope we can keep him there because he is in a lovely place."

Scotti is in no doubt that he belongs. In fact, he suggests there is more to come. Tactically, he can handle the offensive and defensive phases," he explains. "And, regarding his position, I have even seen him play as a central midfielder and do it well."

He adds: "He can adapt to all these positions, which obviously gives him an advantage when it comes to integrating into the squad. The coach can count on him." The signs are that Iraola already does. Not Liverpool's biggest summer signing. But maybe the most important.

articles.title: England to host Netball World Cup in 2031 as tournament heads to Manchester
articles.summary: England to stage Netball World Cup for fourth time, after inaugural edition in Eastbourne in 1963, Birmingham in 1995 and 2019 event in Liverpool; England have claimed bronze medals in two of previous three home World Cups; Manchester's Co-op Live venue for 2031, with 16 teams involved
articles.body:
The nation previously hosted the inaugural edition in 1963 in Eastbourne as well as the 1995 event in Birmingham and 2019 competition in Liverpool.

Sixteen teams will be involved in the World Cup at Manchester's Co-op Live, the venue for this year's Netball Super League Grand Final.

England have claimed bronze medals at two of the previous three World Cups on home soil.

The 2027 World Cup is in Australia next summer, with England out to go one better than their silver medal in South Africa in 2023 and win the competition for the first time.

'We can inspire next generation of players and fans'

On the 2031 tournament, Baroness Sue Campbell, chair of England Netball, said: "As a proud Northerner, I am absolutely thrilled to see the world's biggest netball event coming to Manchester.

"This is a city with an incredible sporting heritage and a real passion for bringing people together through sport.

"To have the best netball players in the world coming to Manchester is a hugely exciting prospect, and I know the city will give them the welcome they deserve.

"This is a fantastic opportunity not only to showcase our sport on the biggest stage, but also to inspire the next generation of players and fans."

World Netball president Dame Liz Nicholl DBE added: "England last hosted our pinnacle event in 2019, for which the legacy still lives on globally through Net2019 legacy projects in Zambia and Argentina, as well as in Great Britain where 160,000 women were inspired to start playing or play more netball because of the event.

"After reviewing their strong bid, I am confident England Netball will host another thrilling international event, and I am excited to see what we can achieve together in 2031 and beyond."

England netball chief executive Fran Connolly said: "[This World Cup] gives us a powerful platform to grow the visibility, profile and impact of women's sport and netball across the UK.

"Having witnessed the spectacle of Netball Super League Grand Final at Co-op Live earlier this summer, we know Manchester is the perfect stage on which to take our sport to another level.

"The energy, atmosphere and ambition we saw in the arena demonstrated what is possible when women's sport is given the platform and investment it deserves.

"Hosting the World Cup in Manchester will allow us to showcase the very best of our sport to a global audience, inspire more people to pick up a netball, and create a lasting legacy for players, fans and communities."

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Martin O'Neill's Celtic on Sky, Rangers eye top spot as Hibs begin Marink Reedijk era
articles.summary: Celtic visit Motherwell live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 11am, seeking a first win in four games; Rangers host Kilmarnock aiming to go top; Marink Reedijk's Hibernian visit Dundee Utd; Hearts play St Mirren, Falkirk take on Dundee and Aberdeen face St Johnstone
articles.body:
Meanwhile, Derek McInnes is hoping to lead Rangers to top spot for the first time and others like St Mirren and Motherwell know positive starts will be undone, should they record four defeats in a row.

Here, we take a look at the big talking points ahead of the weekend…

O'Neill 'raring to go' but will Celtic respond?

Celtic went into the international break on the back of three defeats, two to rivals Rangers and the other in the Europa League.

It left boss Martin O'Neill considering his future and supporters wondering what lay ahead.

The 74-year-old said it didn't take him long to realise he was still up for the challenge of landing the club's sixth consecutive league title, and he was publicly backed by chief executive Michael Nicholson too.

However, for all his legendary status at the club, O'Neill knows he must deliver again if he is to retain the support of those in the stands.

For all that fans have protested against the club's board over transfers and the like - they still expect results. Even if those protests went 72 miles east of Celtic Park during the break, as some supporters threw tennis balls towards principal shareholder Dermot Desmond while he was playing golf at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

Five tricky tests await in the coming weeks, starting with Motherwell at Fir Park on Sunday - live on Sky Sports .

Celtic last suffered four consecutive defeats under Wilfried Nancy last year, a record that had not been matched since 1978. O'Neill knows he must again rewrite the record books for the right reasons, not the wrong. Three points on Sunday is the starting place to deliver that.

Rangers target top spot after tough start

While Celtic have hit a bump in the road after an impressive start, Rangers had to recover from some early teething issues under Derek McInnes before picking up key wins.

The Rangers boss failed to win his first four games in charge and soon after saw the Ibrox side knocked out of Europe by Jablonec .

However, returning from the international break, Rangers have their sights on going top of the Scottish Premiership for the first time this season .

A new-look squad has racked up six consecutive wins across all competitions and McInnes knows that must continue against one of his former clubs on Saturday as Kilmarnock head to Govan.

Victory would take Rangers to the summit, albeit for perhaps only 24 hours, should Celtic then respond against Motherwell on Sunday.

However, it would mark another step in the right direction after a summer that saw the squad overhauled and slowly grow in belief in a quest to land Rangers their first Premiership title since 2021.

Click here for more on the inside story of the club's summer window and why Ibrox chiefs hope it could pave the path to glory.

The Easter Road club went into the break on the search for a new boss after sacking David Gray following their defeat to Kilmarnock .

Eight days after parting ways with their Scottish Cup-winning captain, Marink Reedijk was appointed .

At 35, he is the youngest manager in the top flight and arrives from SK Beveren, where he won the Belgian second-tier title with an unbeaten campaign.

Reedijk, who has also worked in academy positions at Ajax and West Bromwich Albion, took the team to Spain for a training camp during the break and described it as a "pre-season on steroids".

His training sessions appear to be intense and he will be hoping for a reaction on Saturday when they head to Dundee United.

Hibs are winless in four Premiership games, 10th in the table and just two points clear of bottom side Kilmarnock. Reedijk, and the fans, will hope the only way is up.

Heading into the international window, some sides were perhaps looking forward to the break.

Both Motherwell and St Mirren had suffered three straight league defeats after promising starts under Alfred Johansson and Craig McLeish, respectively. However, it doesn't get much easier as the champions head to Fir Park - live on Sky Sports - while the Buddies travel to face Hearts.

Meanwhile, Dundee boss Steven Pressley will have been thankful for the break after seeing his injury list grow.

The Dens Park manager is without at least seven of his starting XI, with three of the absentees out with ACL injuries - namely captain Simon Murray, Jack Moorhouse and Finlay Robertson.

He has added former Man City and Newcastle Utd youngster Alfie Harrison, but more additions from the free agent market might be needed.

articles.title: Thierno Barry's Everton revival? Striker hit rock bottom last season but is working hard to turn his Toffees career around
articles.summary: Thierno Barry has endured some tough moments at Everton but the sight of the striker opening up about his struggles has made supporters more empathetic. Adam Bate speaks to his one-on-one coach to find out more about a man trying to rewrite his story...
articles.body:
Sometimes there is an assumption that every top player is living the dream but when things are not going well, and the whole world is watching, it can feel like a nightmare. "That was real emotion," Scott Chickelday tells Sky Sports . "They were true tears."

Chickelday is the coach who was taking that session with Barry that day, the man trying to coax him into continuing. "He was on the floor when I met him and that video obviously shows it," he says.

Barry's decision to share the footage is an indication in itself that he is in a better place now. But there are still those who might argue that it is a risk in this robust industry to reveal any vulnerability. "It could have gone two ways for him," concedes Chickelday.

But the response has been supportive. "When you play badly as a player you get labelled for picking up your money and not caring. That video, a lot of Everton supporters have looked at it and thought, 'you know what, yes, he does bloody care'."

The very fact that Barry sought out Chickelday says plenty about his desire. He is doing all that he can to succeed. Maybe now he is reaping the rewards. "He has had a big pre-season, putting himself in extra camps to get fit, to get himself mentally tougher."

The result? "He has come back mentally stronger." Barry scored in Everton's opening-weekend victory over Crystal Palace. There was a hat-trick in the cup win at Preston. Last time out, he scored what turned out to be the match-winning goal against Ipswich.

"We worked on his finishing and he has come back flying," says Chickelday, who calls Barry one of the nicest people he has met. "It has been a rollercoaster for him, getting booed by his own fans and being cheered like a hero. All these ups and downs."

He adds: "He has got a young baby too so he has had a lot going on. I know supporters will not look at that side of things because all they see is what he does on a Saturday. But he was adjusting to what is probably one of the toughest leagues in the world."

Barry's whole career must have felt like a whirlwind to him so far. His season in Sochaux's reserves has been followed by one apiece in Belgium, Switzerland, Spain and England. He has already been in Everton's first-team longer than anywhere else.

One recalls speaking to Gunter Vandebroeck, his coach at Beveren in Belgium, prior to his arrival in the Premier League. He talked of a player "hungry and determined" but who still had much to learn. "Tactically, he had a lot to improve." Even now, Barry is only 23.

As such, nobody, Barry included, is under any illusions that he is complete. "He needs repetition, he knows he does," says Chickelday. "But he wants to do it. He still feels like he has got a lot to prove. It has just taken him that bit longer to find his feet."

Barry's extra work with Chickelday is guided by the type of striker that he needs to become in a David Moyes team. "We have to fall in line with that," Chickelday explains. It means focusing on the type of chances that this Everton side might create for him.

"It is about being better in those areas of his game so that when he does find himself in those areas, he is equipped to score. We work a lot on one-touch finishing within the width of the six-yard box. He has just got to get that consistency in his game now."

The reality for Barry is that it is not about the chances that he misses. It is about making sure that he does not allow that misses to impact the next chance. Those grieving moments on the pitch must stop. "It is about being mentally tough," says Chickelday.

"It is about resetting. You have to back yourself. It is the Harry Kane mindset. If you miss an opportunity, that has gone. It is on to the next one. You can still go out there on a Saturday and score goals even if you have not scored in the previous three games.

"Since working with players at this level, that is what I have learned. Talent gets you through the door. Confidence and mindset get you longevity and success. He struggled with that and he needed to get better at it. But he has got better as time has gone."

His body language continues to come under scrutiny but Chickelday believes that can be misleading. "He comes across as this big, confident person when you see his goal celebrations but there are times when he has been low in confidence underneath."

And the statistics certainly suggest that his off-the-ball contribution is significant. Barry ranks among the top-five players in the Premier League this season for both counter pressures and the number of high-speed runs made while pressing the opposition.

The challenge now is for Barry to maintain it. "It is about not having fewer drop offs and becoming more consistent. I am sure that he will. And if he gets it right, he will go on to become a very good striker in the Premier League." This feels like a big opportunity.

Everton do not have many alternatives up front until the January transfer window opens. A chance for Barry to seize the moment. The signs are promising. And, after opening up, the Everton fans are rooting for him too. "He was so low. But he pulled himself back up."

articles.summary: One of the biggest games of the 2026 college football season comes with significant concerns about weather on game day.
articles.body:
One of the biggest games of the 2026 college football season comes with significant concerns about weather on game day.

The Georgia Bulldogs' trip to Tuscaloosa to play the Alabama Crimson Tide will be affected in some capacity by the rains from Hurricane Isaias.

There are no plans to move the biggest game of Week 6, but the conditions could absolutely be a factor inside Bryant-Denny Stadium.

The conditions for most of Saturday's other games are projected to be much better, including the Big Ten clash on the west coast between the UCLA Bruins and Oregon Ducks.

All of the forecasts for Week 6's top college football games can be found here on The Weather Channel.

Week 6 Top 25 Schedule, Odds and Weather

Forecast: Mostly Cloudy, Chance of Rain, High of 61°F

North Carolina at No. 25 Pittsburgh (-3.5)

Prediction: Pittsburgh 31, North Carolina 17

South Carolina at No. 16 Florida (-12.5)

Prediction: Florida 24, South Carolina 10

No. 1 Texas (-7.5) vs. Oklahoma (Game in Dallas)

Forecast: Chance of Showers, High of 81°F

Forecast: Chance of Showers, High of 80°F

Forecast: Showers and Windy, High of 77°F

No. 23 Boise State (-6.5) at Fresno State

Prediction: Boise State 34, Fresno State 20

A good amount of the talk building up to the Georgia-Alabama clash has been about the weather.

Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the southeast, but as of Wednesday night, the game is still on in Tuscaloosa, per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.

Showers are in the forecast for most of Saturday, but come Saturday night, there is only a 40 percent chance of rain.

The wet conditions would lead many people to lean with the Under 51.5 from a betting perspective.

The under might have even been in play in perfect conditions. Georgia hasn't allowed over 20 points this season, while Alabama's held four of its five opponents to 23 points or fewer.

Georgia owns the seventh-best team defense in the FBS. The Bulldogs allow just 244.6 yards per game. That number will be tested by the two-way dynamic play of Keelon Russell.

The one weakness between the two defenses is the Alabama secondary, which has allowed 234 passing yards per game.

Gunner Stockton comes into Saturday with a completion percentage of 75.5, 13 passing touchdowns and just one interception across UGA's five victories.

Stockton also owns the edge in experience over Russell. The multi-year UGA starting quarterback had 15 passing touchdowns and two interceptions in six games against Top 25 opposition last season. He had four touchdown throws in two games versus Alabama in 2025.

Russell has proved that he is capable of handling the big moments so far as the Bama starting quarterback, but this will be his toughest test yet, and he might not be able to lead the Tide past a UGA team with a stout defense and one of the more experienced signal-callers in the SEC.

The Oregon Ducks will play their second straight west coast opponent from the Big Ten on Saturday.

Oregon beat the USC Trojans two weeks ago thanks to Dylan Raiola's standout showing in place of the injured Dante Moore.

Moore is not expected to be available for the Week 6 clash with the UCLA Bruins, per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.

The oddsmakers still have Oregon as an 11.5-point favorite despite Moore being out. Raiola threw for 269 yards and a pair of touchdowns against USC.

UCLA comes into Eugene at 4-0 with three 45-plus-point performances, led by quarterback Nico Iamaleava.

Oregon is the first Top 25 opponent the Bruins will face, but there's still the potential to put up points. The Ducks let up at least 27 points to all three of their FBS opponents this season.

Raiola and Iamaleava could each have big days against two defenses that give up over 300 total yards per game.

Oregon has the better talent on paper, but it's a bit difficult to back it as a double-digit favorite until its defense plays better.

In this case, the Over 58.5 is the better look because we know for sure that both offenses can move the ball well and put up points.

Expert CFB Predictions for the Biggest Week 6 Games 🔒

Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns are 10-1 in their last 11 games, a run that started in last year's Red River Rivalry game against the Oklahoma Sooners.

Manning, Cam Coleman and Co. are off to a 4-0 start that includes a home win over the Ohio State Buckeyes and a tough road win over the Tennessee Volunteers.

It's no surprise to see the Longhorns as a 7.5-point favorite against the Sooners because of their early-season results.

Texas is 3-1 in its last four meetings with Oklahoma. The Sooners scored nine points across those three defeats.

A bet on Texas at 7.5 points seems quite easy to make if you consider the September results, the historical trends and the team's defensive numbers in 2026.

Texas held three of its four opponents to 17 points or fewer. It is one of 14 FBS teams to allow 13 points per game or fewer.

Oklahoma struggled in its two biggest games of the season to date, both of which ended up in losses.

The Sooners were outclassed by the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs by a 41-13 score and they mustered just 10 points on the road against the Michigan Wolverines.

Upsets are always a possibility in rivalry games, but it feels like the chips are stacked against Oklahoma in this specific matchup.
