articles.body:
For those in search of a weird, chaotic week of college football, look no further.

All of the ingredients are in place for Week 6. This theme extends up and down the odds board.

Translation: prepare for upsets. Lots of 'em.

In the SEC, we've got our eye on Alabama-Georgia, with the impending weather. In the Big Ten, we want to see what the defending national champions have in store for their first meaningful road trip of the year.

Given our performance last week (finally), we welcome the possibility of chaos with open arms.

We're heating up. A solid winning week could have been even better, although we won't complain about the results. Instead, we're hoping to build on it moving forward.

The game itself is blanketed in intrigue, although there's a lot to unpack first.

A tropical storm in the gulf has put this game squarely in jeopardy. By the time you read this, this football game may or may not still be on the schedule, which is a very simplified way of explaining a very complicated situation.

Still, for now, we're breaking it down. Of course we are. It's Alabama vs. Georgia.

The numbers say this will be a magnificent football game. They also tell us that the scoreboard will stay busy, although the conditions could have a say in that.

Presently. Georgia has the nation's No. 1 scoring offense. Alabama, which has faced better competition through five weeks, is No. 3.

As for the competition, Georgia has certainly seen the level of competition pick up of late, dominating Oklahoma and most recently Vanderbilt. Alabama has scored at least 45 points in every game this season. The Crimson Tide just dropped a cool 56 points on Mississippi State.

The quarterbacks for both teams are spectacular. Alabama's Keelon Russell and Georgia's Gunner Stockton have combined to score15 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions.

There's a bit of volatility to Alabama's playing style, which could work for or against this team. The first half against Mississippi State was turnover-centric, and that's certainly a concern while playing against a team as good as Georgia.

But this volatility also amounts to explosiveness, and Russell is showing the ability to take over a game more than any player in college football not named Jeremiah Smith.

Again, we hope this game is played. We also hope everyone is safe. We're taking Alabama and keeping our eye on what happens next.

Let's be brutally honest for a moment, shall we?

The level of competition these two teams have faced through five weeks of football is frankly alarming. Neither opponent has faced a ranked team, although Indiana's win over Northwestern, which looked iffy at the time, looks solid a few weeks later.

With that acknowledged, it's safe to say we are processing both teams.

Indiana is, well, Indiana. The pieces are still coming together, though the talent level clearly isn't what it was last year. That doesn't mean this team can't be good—we liked them enough to pick them here.

Last week, even against Rutgers, the pieces looked better. Quarterback Josh Hoover was efficient, running back Turbo Richard was explosive and the defense was solid.

Playing on the road this week won't be easy, especially in an environment that should be overflowing, but Curt Cignetti has proven just how much of a difference his presence can make.

Slowing down Nebraska QB Anthony Colandrea won't be an easy assignment. He threw for three touchdowns and ran for 108 yards last week, which will give Indiana plenty to think about.

Still, the Hoosiers are proven. They've played in tough environments before. Perhaps this is the week Nebraska finally breaks through, although it feels like a tall task.

There's a theme that has carried through the SEC over the past month.

Win a big game, celebrate said big win, and then lose horribly the following week. Ole Miss knows how this feels. Now, Florida does, too. Missouri, coming off an absolute throttling of the Gators, will have to shake off that success and take on a rejuvenated Texas A&M group.

Granted, the Aggies just played Arkansas. Given the state of that program, they'll essentially rejuvenate every team they play. (Sorry, Arkansas fans.)

Still, given A&M's up-and-down play this season, this spread feels a little light. Given how superb the Tigers looked this weekend, they're likely to be a very public play.

Speaking of ups and downs, enter Marcel Reed. While his improved play came against an inferior opponent, the game plan worked. Quick throws, keep him moving and don't ask him to do too much. That's the formula.

As for Missouri, let's not lose perspective. The prior week, we saw the Tigers collapse against Mississippi State late. That's not to diminish anything that was just done; it's merely to provide some perspective of how quickly things can change.

Football hangovers work in mysterious ways. Sometimes, a massive win can result in a deflating next game. Sometimes, an emotional week (and loss) can linger longer than expected.

That brings us to Iowa, which put a lot of emotion into its game against Ohio State. ESPN's College Gameday visited the school for the first time in two decades. The hoopla surrounding their matchup against the Buckeyes felt real.

The Hawkeyes hung around for a while. Eventually, however, Jeremiah Smith and overall talent took over.

Now, Iowa must travel cross-country for a Friday night game, which feels like a recipe for trouble.

Granted, Washington hasn't exactly performed up to expectations. Back-to-back losses to Minnesota and USC have this team reeling. The Huskies didn't exactly overwhelm the competition in the three prior wins.

Quarterback Demond Williams Jr. still produced a few jaw-dropping plays in the loss to the Trojans. He's more than capable of producing enough offense.

With a total that is likely to hover around 41, don't expect an offensive surge. Iowa has struggled on that front lately. It doesn't bode well for a road trip like this.

Over the past few weeks, P.J. Fleck has been a content machine. He's also won two very important football games, beating Washington, which we discussed, and Michigan.

Suddenly, an ugly loss to Mississippi State feels like a distant memory.

Despite the last few wins, the oddsmakers aren't as convinced. Or perhaps they're giving Purdue plenty of credit despite a 2-3 record. As they should.

When you look at the Boilermakers' schedule, it makes sense. The three losses came against Wake Forest, UCLA and Notre Dame. All three teams have shown plenty of positive signs thus far.

Purdue also just beat Illinois on the road, winning outright as nearly a double-digit underdog. Quarterback Ryan Browne has been a nice surprise thus far, throwing for eight touchdowns and just one interception.

In many respects, this one is a product of both competition and timing. While Minnesota has been playing well, this is a tricky road trip before a bye after two absolute thrillers.

Expect the Boilermakers to take full advantage and win outright as a small underdog.

To be clear, this football game has a high probability of being grotesque.

The total has dipped below 40. It's not hard to see why. For as much offense as we'll see in Alabama-Georgia, this one could feature quite the opposite.

Oklahoma is currently No. 109 in scoring offense. Things have been bleak lately. In the past three games, the Sooners have scored 29 points. Granted, two of those games came against Georgia and Michigan—two outstanding defenses. But that disclaimer only goes so far.

By comparison, Texas has been better. Still, the Longhorns are No. 55 in scoring offense. The many talented pieces on that side of the ball haven't exactly gelled. Despite that, Texas still has impressive wins over Ohio State and Tennessee.

That brings us to this matchup, which will be played on a neutral site, surrounded by fried food. Both teams enjoyed a bye last week, which likely meant more for Oklahoma given its current state.

One week isn't enough time to cure John Mateer's woes, although it can't hurt. The offense has to be better, as running the football will certainly help. It'll be difficult to do so consistently against this Texas front, although that thought will work both ways.

The end result will be a slog of a football game that Texas will ultimately win to stay unbeaten. Oklahoma, however, will do its part to keep it ugly enough.

On the topic of point spreads that grabbed our attention, enter Utah State. The spread seems off, but consider the following. The Aggies have already played road games at Washington, Utah and Boise State.

With QB Mason Heintschel out for the year, Holden Geriner will take over for Pittsburgh. That's certainly a big deal, although North Carolina is quietly playing significantly improved football, no matter what the record says.

We faded West Virginia last week at Iowa State, which resulted in a push. Despite how well Arizona played against unbeaten Cincinnati, this feels like a tricky road trip against an offense that can move the ball.

To say Georgia Tech has played underwhelming football would be an understatement. Let's not forget, however, that Duke struggled against a struggling Illinois team earlier in the year. This one will be tight.

articles.title: Every Premier League Team's Biggest Flaw So Far for the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: We're five games into the 2026-27 Premier League season, and while teams are still figuring out their identity as they chase their respective targets for the campaign, there are plenty of positives to pick out.
articles.body:
We're five games into the 2026-27 Premier League season, and while teams are still figuring out their identity as they chase their respective targets for the campaign, there are plenty of positives to pick out.

Manchester City are adapting seamlessly to life under new boss Enzo Maresca. Brentford have continued to build on last season's success under the guidance of Keith Andrews. Leeds United have taken things up a notch after securing survival. And Hull City are defying expectations with a low-block and route-one style that makes them frustratingly difficult to beat.

But there are lots of negatives, too, from leaky defenses to stuttering attacks and everything in between.

Ahead, Nick Akerman, Calum Rogers, and Leo Collis have run the rule over every Premier League team and found the biggest flaw of each so far in the young season.

Anything they've missed? Leave your thoughts in the comments.

Arsenal spent much of the summer in widely reported chases for Vinícius Júnior and then Julián Alvarez in a bid to upgrade the team's attack. But after losing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, the only addition to the team's forward line was Christos Tzolis.

The 24-year-old has had a somewhat promising start, but it's still difficult to consider him much of an upgrade over Trossard and Martinelli. So far, Arsenal have had to grind out a couple of tough away games against Aston Villa and Sunderland and were blown away by Brighton and Hove Albion prior to the break.

To make matters worse, Tzolis and Kai Havertz have both picked up injuries over the break that seem likely to at least leave them sidelined for a few weeks. Viktor Gyökeres has only played just over 100 minutes across the Premier League and Champions League this season, and he will now need to swiftly regain Mikel Arteta's trust.

Given recent events concerning fellow challengers Manchester City, Arsenal's attack may not need to be that good to secure another Premier League title. But this group should receive a significant upgrade within the next year, and the Gunners' recruitment work suggests they agree.

In May, he won the Europa League with Aston Villa — an incredible achievement built on a squad with a world-class spine. A few months later, that backbone was decimated, forcing the manager into a quick rebuild after losing key players Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa, Luca Digne, and Emi Martinez.

Despite last weekend's win over last-placed Tottenham, early signs suggest that Emery will be forced to use a number of players whom he didn't fancy last season in greater roles.

Victor Lindelof currently has more minutes on the pitch than any other player, and Ross Barkley has made four starts. It's a serious drop in base quality, with players who are meant to be cup fodder now playing important matches.

Emery is very good at working things out — perhaps too good, making it easier for the board to leave him understaffed. The ceiling has dropped at a time when Villa's schedule has increased with Champions League football, a backward step when the club needed to build on the success of last season.

Bournemouth have dropped nine points from winning positions already this season. Those dropped points would have them level with second-placed Arsenal, but instead they're down in 17th.

The Cherries have also already conceded four goals from the 80th minute onward, and those struggles late in games could be a concern they continue to deal with as their squad gets stretched by Europa League football. Star midfielder Alex Scott has picked up an injury on international duty too, depleting his team further ahead of a run of nine games in 28 days.

Bournemouth dropped the second-most points from winning positions last season too, so this isn't a new problem, and it may be that their frenetic style makes it difficult to slow games down when they have the advantage. It was an issue former manager Andoni Iraola never quite got to grips with on the south coast, and his replacement Marco Rose will have little doubt that he needs to find answers after some heartbreaking late goals against so far.

His team has shown enough promise that there's little need to panic about their slow start, but improving their ability to hold onto leads would make a massive difference.

Brentford: Failing to Get Igor Thiago Involved

Brentford's 2025-26 campaign, which took them to an impressive ninth place, was largely built on Igor Thiago, with the Brazilian notching 22 of the Bees' 55 goals (40%).

His lone goal this season, coming against Chelsea just before the international break, accounts for just 10% of Brentford's successful strikes.

Meanwhile, Fotmob has Thiago on just 23 touches inside the opposition box, or just 4.6 per game, and he's had just four shots on target from 13 attempts.

While it's definitely encouraged that manager Keith Andrews relies a little less on the big No. 9 for their scoring output—with the Brazilian increasingly man-marked and other players getting more space as a result—Thiago should be getting more of a sniff to help the Bees turn draws (three out of five) into victories.

Brentford's approach has so far proved effective, sitting fourth in the table in the early going and still yet to taste defeat, but getting Thiago involved a little more could make them even more convincing. Opening his account in the last game against the Blues might prove to be the kickstart he needed.

It's quite difficult to pick out many flaws with Brighton.

Fabian Hürzeler's side sit third in the Premier League, are the division's top scorers with 16, and thrashed champions Arsenal 3-0 last time out. Oh, and don't forget the Seagulls became the first team to overturn a 2-0 halftime deficit away at Manchester United in 41 years when they won 3-2 in the League Cup earlier this month.

They are, by all means, playing very good football, led by the division's best player right now, Pascal Groß. However, Hürzeler will be well aware that his side tends to start games slowly, conceding too many goals in the opening exchanges.

Roméo Lavia and Pedro Neto had Chelsea 2-0 up within 15 minutes during the first game of the season, with João Pedro adding a third just after the half-hour mark. Brighton had 75% possession and lost 4-3. Jaden Bogle scored in 15 minutes during the next match, a 1-1 draw with Leeds. Shea Lacy and Mason Mount put Man United 2-0 up in 10 minutes at Old Trafford.

While Brighton have shown they are more than capable of fighting back, it's not sustainable to start each match with a deficit, particularly with European football starting when the international break concludes.

Xabi Alonso's Chelsea have conceded more goals than any other side in the Premier League after five matches. Twelve is worse than all three of the promoted clubs, including Ipswich, who shipped five in one match against Man United.

The strength of Chelsea's front three is keeping them in games, but we saw a real dip in potency when João Pedro missed the defeat to Brentford through injury. Both Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer seemed off the pace and could only watch on as the Bees strolled to a momentous 3-0 win that laid bare the issues Alonso needs to address.

His transitional 3-4-3 is typically hard to execute well in the Premier League. Alonso continues to experiment with his wingbacks in search of the Alex Grimaldo and Jeremie Frimpong of his invincible Bundesliga season with Bayer Leverkusen, but he just doesn't have that lightning-in-a-bottle quality at his disposal.

Part of the issue comes down to the center-backs. While Maxence Lacroix looks a good signing, stationing him between Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana doesn't seem properly balanced. There are no defining traits in the latter two that suggest they could be beaten in a race or in the air by many forwards in the league.

That lack of personality is an issue when Alonso's formation forces everyone to be at the top of their game and exposes anyone who isn't. Like Ruben Amorim's Man United last year, the coach can't be passive about improving their leaky rear end. It'll undermine Chelsea's entire campaign if he is.

Coventry City finally got their first Premier League win since 2001 last time out, with Jay Dasilva breaking free on the left side and finishing with aplomb against Nottingham Forest.

In addition to marking their first three points of the campaign, Dasilva scored the Sky Blues' first goal of the season.

Among a host of incoming players in the summer, preparing for the rigors of top-flight football, a reliable goalscorer was sadly overlooked. Sidiki Cherif might turn out well eventually, but relying on a 19-year-old to carry the scoring burden in his first year of English football might not have been the best strategy. Taiwo Awoniyi, meanwhile, does have Premier League experience, but he hasn't hit double figures in goals in the division since 2022-23.

Haji Wright, who scored 45 goals for Coventry in three seasons in the Championship, might not be back until November after dealing with a thigh problem, and even then, he'll need some time to get up to speed.

The West Midlanders will take confidence from the victory over Forest, but the international break could scupper any momentum. Coventry will need to find goals from somewhere if they have any hope of extending their Premier League stay.

Crystal Palace's domestic home form is pretty worrying.

The Eagles have played two at Selhurst Park this season, conceding seven and accumulating zero points. It's early days, but Pierre Sage has been unable to halt a pattern that saw Oliver Glasner out the door. His team appears tentative to perform in front of their own fans.

It's actually been five home Premier League games without a win if we stretch back to last season. Perhaps it's the quality of the division, because we've seen Palace batter Middlesbrough and Lech Poznan in cup competitions this campaign.

Maybe it's the lack of support from the Holdmesdale Fanatics, who stopped their brilliant, banner-laden frenzy in August out of anger over how the club is treating its fans.

Something is missing when Palace play at Selhurst Park. With one win in five to begin the season, they need to sort it out soon, or else slip into a relegation battle that they may not be equipped to escape.

Everton's unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign comes despite a pretty disastrous transfer window that left David Moyes' squad severely lacking with just 15 senior players.

God forbid Thierno Barry gets injured; the Toffees simply don't have a backup striker after letting Beto leave without securing a replacement on deadline day.

His form has summed up the Merseyside club pretty well; the Frenchman's performance level has increased massively through the first five games, where he's working hard, fighting for every ball and finishing more of the chances that fall his way.

There's a gutsiness to Everton at the moment. They know what people are saying about them; James Tarkowski even noted the outside "noise" during a recent interview. They're sticking together and putting in an excellent shift so far. Just nobody gets injured until at least January.

Things just haven't seemed quite right for Fulham this season. The Press Association described a "social media revolt" in early September that involved players appearing to cryptically express displeasure with the club.

It is worth acknowledging that two of the players, Kevin and Emile Smith-Rowe, have barely featured under new manager Alvaro Arbeloa, but it is concerning how readily they appeared to make their dissatisfaction public.

Perhaps this is all a storm in a teacup that can be resolved by unhappy players being moved on and some improved results—since the controversy, Fulham have drawn with both Liverpool and Manchester United and beaten West Ham United in the Carabao Cup.

But there are concerns about the dressing-room tensions during Arbeloa's time at Real Madrid. BBC Sport reported that Federico Valverde required hospital treatment following a disagreement with teammate Aurélien Tchouaméni, although Valverde denied that either player struck the other and said he accidentally hit a table.

After having only collected two points from five games, pressure is building on the Spaniard, and a recovery will only become more difficult if he doesn't have the backing of his players.

Hull City fans are probably sick of hearing about "expected goal" numbers. According to Opta Analyst , the Tigers were the second-worst team in the Championship last season in expected points. If things played out based on how those metrics value chances created and surrendered, Hull would've been relegated to League 1 rather than promoted to the Premier League.

Their overperformance hasn't been quite as stark this season, but Understat 's expected points model has them in 15th, just above Tottenham Hotspur and well below their actual standing of eighth.

These models aren't perfect for assessing a team's quality. There are various factors that can affect an xG total, and a sample size of five games is also too small to draw any significant conclusions.

However, we do know that Hull came into this season looking likely to face a battle to avoid relegation, and the underlying numbers still place them in that range.

Tigers fans have every right to sneer at these projections at this point, and I will gladly accept that I was one of many prognosticators to underestimate them entering the season. But as much as I hate to harsh anyone's buzz, there's still every possibility that things start to tail off even after a spectacular start.

In Ipswich Town's last stint in the Premier League, they didn't pick up a win until November. This time around, they've got two in just five matches, suggesting things might go a little better in 2026-27.

One key to survival will be stopping goals from going in. The Tractor Boys are one of four teams yet to keep a clean sheet, and the only promoted side not to do so.

Shoring up the back line is absolutely crucial, especially as teams start to find their footing and chart effective routes to goal.

Addressing that area of the pitch in January might be sensible, but there are plenty of games to go until the window opens. Finding solutions internally, such as swapping Sasa Lukic for a more mobile destroyer in Florentino or switching to a back five, could plug the leak until a more permanent solution is found.

Leeds United: Having No Calvert-Lewin Backup

Leeds don't have a lot to complain about. They're third in the league, and while that position is unlikely to hold come the end of the season, FotMob's expected-goal numbers still place them firmly in the top half of the table.

So, rather than try to pick holes in what's been a dream start for the Lilywhites, the biggest issue for Leeds is a hypothetical one: the health of striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who scored 14 league goals last season and is on pace for a similar total this season.

Lukas Nmecha would be the most likely player to step in if Calvert-Lewin were unavailable, but the 27-year-old has failed to hold down a starting spot for much of his career, making it difficult to have much faith in his ability to do so in the Premier League.

The club is well aware of the potential issue too. In quotes reported by The Athletic , managing director Robbie Evans explained the difficulty of finding a backup for Calvert-Lewin: "Supporting roles are quite hard to fill because you have to have this Venn diagram: overlapping circles of the right character, the right squad fit, the right price, and be content to be a backup."

"... The number of players who are good enough to play in the league, willing to fight for their spot or be a backup, and fit our long-term profile financially is a very, very small list."

If Leeds can put together another strong season, that list of potential targets could grow. But that possibility will rest squarely on the 29-year-old Calvert-Lewin's availability.

Liverpool are still figuring things out under Andoni Iraola. The Spaniard hasn't quite implemented the hard-pressing, attacking football we saw while he was at Bournemouth, although there have been occasional glimmers of that approach.

Fitness could be an issue, as could adaptation within the squad. But most of all, a sizeable gap in the middle of the park seems to be hurting fluidity and cohesion.

Ryan Gravenberch is out of favor, having started just twice in the Premier League so far. Alexis Mac Allister has improved after taking a step back last season, but he still looks a little bit overwhelmed. Meanwhile, Dominik Szoboszlai has been putting in the hard yards, but when he's in possession, he keeps picking the wrong pass.

As for Florian Wirtz, he still doesn't look up to the task physically, and the line-breaking passes and delicate touches he's capable of remain shockingly absent in his Liverpool career.

Elsewhere, though, the defense looks reborn with Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo, while up front, Alexander Isak has rediscovered his scoring form and Cody Gakpo is a completely different player compared to last season.

The left-hand side still needs some work, with Milos Kerkez erratic and Bradley Barcola adapting, but that midfield chasm is the glaring weakness, and it's harming improvements elsewhere in the XI.

Finding a flaw for the only team with a 100 percent record and one that's sitting at the top of the table is a difficult task.

Concerns over the transition from Pep Guardiola to Enzo Maresca have so far proved overblown, with the Italian manager overseeing a minor rebuild while still picking up impressive wins. Granted, the biggest test so far has been a Manchester derby against neighbors who are in disarray, so maybe we shouldn't be naming them champions-elect just yet.

While Maresca's teams aren't known for swarming all over the pitch, it's still surprising that his side has covered the third-least distance in the Premier League so far this season, running more than seven kilometers per match less than title-holders Arsenal, according to Fotmob .

There is something to be said for effortless control over aimless running, and the approach is obviously proving successful so far. But as teams improve their fitness as the season progresses, City could soon be put under increasing duress with little energy in the tank to respond.

This entire article could be dedicated to Manchester United's flaws. It could have been the full-backs or the inability to break down defenses. Perhaps even Michael Carrick himself could have taken the headline. In typical United fashion, something far more wide-reaching appears to be the main issue.

The Red Devils are just not running. As Sky Sports' stats detailed after the 1-1 draw with Fulham, the squad's out-of-possession numbers are a dismal blend of not working hard enough and ineffective running when they do up the ante. Last in distance at high intensity, last in sprints, 17th in time spent walking.

There may be few confirmed links between these stats and winning matches, but the eye test reveals a lot. United find it hard to shift between gears. The walking at Craven Cottage let Fulham stroll as well, opening up easy passes from the back. Alvaro Arbeloa's side finally looked comfortable in his possession-based style. No other team has let that happen.

United upped their effort after falling behind. Luke Shaw finally ran beyond Marcus Rashford, providing a crossing angle that had otherwise been neglected. Players started to run beyond their markers.

Whether the upped energy was effective or not, it created openings and a greater intensity to claw back a 1-1 draw. Carrick needs more before he's led to the exit.

Between the departures of manager Eddie Howe and long-tenured players Bruno Guimarães, Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Kieran Trippier, Newcastle United lost almost 850 games of experience on Tyneside over the summer.

The response to that was to hire a manager in Matthias Jaissle who has never managed in a top European league and to supply him largely with signings aged 24 and under, and with only Nico Gonzalez possessing any Premier League experience.

It was a bold strategy, and results so far have been mixed. The Magpies do sit ninth, but Understat 's expected points model has them as the second-worst team so far based on the quality of chances they've created and surrendered.

The concerns about Newcastle's lack of experience were brought into sharp focus in the 4-1 defeat to Leeds United. Nico was forced off early with an injury, leaving Jaissle to cobble together a midfield of Lewis Miley (20 years old) and Sean Stur (18). Both players struggled to cope with the intensity of the game, and it left their teammates horribly exposed defensively.

It's still early days, and the fact that Newcastle have still picked up results amid all the upheaval this season is some cause for optimism. But there is also enough reason to worry that their recruitment strategy may have left them exposed in a league where experience and physicality are becoming ever more crucial.

Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest are 13th in the Premier League, with two wins, two losses and a draw from five games. Only Coventry and Spurs have scored fewer than their four goals. Yet, nobody outside the top eight has conceded fewer goals. They've drawn with Liverpool, beaten Villa, and lost to Coventry.

All of this is to say, Glasner's first few weeks in charge have been wildly inconsistent. He's a demanding coach who brings a new 3-4-2-1 formation to the club, sure, but the differences in Forest's performances have been as wide as the results.

Perhaps a greater sample size is needed before judgment goes too deep on this team. Glasner sides tend to get rolling after a while. Forest have real quality packed into the starting XI, with Morgan Gibbs-White, Daniel Muñoz and others who speak to the Glasner way of playing.

Right now, it's hard to tell whether the team is going to fight for a great result or throw a match away, a pattern that needs to become just a quirk of the new tenure getting up to speed, rather than a character flaw in the squad.

It might not be so obvious, given Sunderland got three past Manchester City last time out in a 5-3 defeat, but the Black Cats aren't making the most of their big chances.

According to Fotmob , the 15 notable opportunities the Wearsiders have spurned account for the most in the Premier League, two more than Brighton & Hove Albion and Crystal Palace in joint second.

What makes that figure even more disappointing, compared with the Seagulls, is that the south-coasters have scored 16, while the Black Cats have just six goals (half of them against City).

It's not just down to one player, either. Five players have missed two big chances each, while another five have also spurned one major goal opportunity.

Sunderland haven't gotten off to the same fast start as last season, when they were up to seventh after five games and had picked up eight points—they are 14th and have four points after five games in 2026-27. Making the most of those big chances is imperative to ensure that they don't regress.

The selection here was not difficult: Tottenham's record of five Premier League games played and two goals scored would be shocking even if they hadn't spent over $400 million supposedly upgrading the team over the summer.

Spurs will be hoping things improve as players get to grips with Roberto De Zerbi's detailed instructions in possession. The worry, though, is that there simply isn't enough attacking productivity in the team for there to be a high ceiling even if that does happen.

Strikers Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush have just three double-digit top-flight goalscoring seasons between them. Solanke last reached that milestone for Bournemouth in the 2023-24 season, and Marmoush has never done so outside of the Bundesliga. Wingers Savio, Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus also only had 15 goals between them over the previous two Premier League seasons.

It all makes the decision to leave Richarlison out of the Premier League squad all the more confusing. The Brazilian is not a perfect player, but he is the best pure penalty box threat Spurs have and was their top scorer last season. So far, his omission looks like one of the most questionable decisions in a summer full of them.

articles.title: Tottenham Sky Sports special podcast: Tim Sherwood and Michael Bridge assess Spurs' problems after winless start
articles.summary: In a special Sky Sports Spurs podcast, Tim Sherwood and Sky Sports News' Tottenham reporter Michael Bridge assess the club's winless start to the Premier League season, which has left them bottom; watch Man Utd vs Spurs on Saturday, live on Sky Sports; kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
That's because it has been nearly two years since Spurs have won a match after conceding the opening goal in any competition. Last month's 3-2 home loss to Villa was the 47th game in this dismal run (D11 L36).

"It is a worry, certainly at home because that's where you need the minerals," former Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood told a special Sky Sports Spurs podcast.

"That's where you need the characters and leaders to come forward, and at the moment, they're void of any leaders and characters.

"I'm not sure there's anyone really losing their head or galvanising the players to try and arrest [it], which is a poor trend, in not fighting back from losing positions.

"The manager is. He certainly looks like he doesn't lack in any passion. But you need that within the pitch and within the dressing room and within the training pitch every single day, and I'm not sure the characters are there."

With Spurs accumulating the fewest points (18) among ever-present Premier League sides in 2026, Sky Sports News' Tottenham reporter Michael Bridge aired his concerns over leadership too.

He said: "When Roberto De Zerbi chose his five captains [Micky van de Ven, Pedro Porro, Ben Davies, James Maddison and Archie Gray], and I asked him in the press conference, Andy Robertson wasn't one of the five.

"Archie Gray was, but Archie Gray's not going to be in the team much, so I am a little bit worried about leadership in that camp.

"How many of the players are really going to grab each other by the scruff of the neck?

"Cristian Romero maybe went too far in terms of aggression, but there were times when you did want him on your side, so I need to see a bit more aggression from some of these players as well."

A winless start to the Premier League season has left Tottenham bottom of the table, and their worst start to a Premier League season after five games has already raised questions over Spurs' lavish summer spending.

So, have any of the 10 new players that cost over £330m impressed Sherwood?

"No, no one," he insisted. "I can't say anyone's really impressed me, and anyone would have done a better job than anyone who was there last season.

"They've underachieved, they really have. We always judge on results, so I don't look at any individual player and think, 'Well, you're coming out of some credit here', because the team's losing, and I'm not sure there's been any outstanding performers."

The lack of success from Spurs' signings before this summer worries Sherwood about the latest recruits.

"Probably the last four or five years, the track record of Tottenham signings has not been fantastic," he said.

"It's been a very long time since they've made a decent signing. Now, I'm not saying they're poor signings; I'm saying that they haven't done it yet, and there's still a lot of time to be able to get some confidence and show what they can really do.

"We've seen them in fits and starts and little cameos for other teams, but it's a different kettle of fish playing for Tottenham."

He added: "I've seen more nos than yeses at the moment over the last five years in the transfer market.

"I think the best signing they've made in recent history would have to be (Heung-Min) Son - and we're going way back there! We're talking about a real success.

"Maybe (Dejan) Kulusevski, but then he's picked up the injury. But other than that, I can't say there have been too many outstanding successes in the transfer market.

"But it's up to Roberto De Zerbi to develop them players, and hopefully some of these players we've seen in recent years can be unrecognisable."

With Spurs having scored just two league goals, the spotlight for Bridge is on Omar Marmoush to deliver.

The summer signing from Man City is yet to score in his first five Spurs appearances in all competitions, having missed one big chance and had two shots on target from his 10 attempts.

Bridge said: "I think the one for me is Omar Marmoush. How good is this guy?

"I really liked glimpses of him for City, but they were only glimpses; clearly a very talented player. He really showed it in the Bundesliga [with Eintracht Frankfurt].

"But can he do it consistently for Tottenham Hotspur, where he's going to be given a clear run of games.

"Were Tottenham right to spend as they did on Savio and Marmoush? So the jury's going to be out with these players."

With Dominic Solanke struggling for form and Richarlison frozen out against the backdrop of Spurs academy graduate Will Lankshear scoring freely in the Championship, Spurs' firepower is a problem.

Bridge said: "I think they need a striker - an actual number nine - but how many are there out there?

"It doesn't help that Will Lankshear is scoring every week for Middlesbrough because he looks like a proper old-fashioned centre-forward and he's young and English. That's my worry.

"I'm also not one hundred per cent sure if Antonin Kinsky is a Tottenham number one for years to come.

"If you've spent that amount of money and you still need, for me, a goalkeeper and a number nine, then there's still a way to go."

Tottenham aim for their first league win of the season at Manchester United on Saturday, live on Sky Sports .

But should their winless run continue, then Roberto De Zerbi would become just the second Spurs boss in Premier League history to fail to win any of the opening six games of a campaign.

Juande Ramos was the first, and he was sacked after Spurs had two points from eight games. But both Sherwood and Bridge are confident that De Zerbi will not follow the same fate as the Spaniard.

Ex-Spurs boss Sherwood said: "I'm not sure he's under pressure because they've given him everything he wanted, so they must have full trust in him.

"He's proven that he's a very good Premier League manager, albeit he's never been at a club the size of Tottenham Hotspur, with the scrutiny which is upon the club, but he looks like a character who can handle that scrutiny, and he just needs a win."

Bridge said: "I don't think Roberto De Zerbi is under much pressure at all.

"He was tracked by the club for some time. He's on a very good and long contract, and unless he's the one that initiates the departure, I don't see any change for the foreseeable."

But what has to change is Spurs' bouncebackability in games if De Zerbi is to ensure the pressure does not mount.

articles.title: Tan sólo una semana de castigo para Álex Sola
articles.standfirst: El club confirma que el jugador volverá a la dinámica del primer equipo el próximo lunes tras cumplir la sanción disciplinaria
articles.summary: El club confirma que el jugador volverá a la dinámica del primer equipo el próximo lunes tras cumplir la sanción disciplinaria
articles.body: El caso Álex Sola sigue dejando nuevos capítulos prácticamente a diario. El último, y el que parece poner punto final al asunto tras la primera manifestación pública de la UD Almería, es la fecha del regreso del futbolista a la dinámica del primer equipo. El club rojiblanco ha informado este jueves de que el jugador volverá a entrenarse con normalidad junto al resto de sus compañeros el próximo lunes, una vez concluya el periodo de sanción interna que le ha mantenido apartado durante toda esta semana. La entidad ha querido aclarar públicamente la situación del futbolista, recordando que su ausencia de los entrenamientos responde exclusivamente a "motivos disciplinarios". Tras los acontecimientos ocurridos el pasado domingo, el Almería activó su régimen disciplinario interno y decidió apartarlo temporalmente de la dinámica del grupo mientras cumplía la sanción impuesta. Durante estos días, Álex Sola ha continuado ejercitándose en las instalaciones del club siguiendo un plan de trabajo individual, sin participar en las sesiones dirigidas por García Pimienta junto al resto de la plantilla. Con este comunicado, el Almería da prácticamente por cerrado el episodio disciplinario en el plano deportivo. El jugador se perderá el encuentro de este domingo frente al Leganés y regresará el lunes a los entrenamientos colectivos, una decisión que ha sorprendido a buena parte del entorno rojiblanco después de que se hablara de una "sanción sin precedentes", que finalmente se queda tan sólo un pequeño escalón por encima de la que recibió Aridane Hernández hace menos de un año por un episodio de características similares. En aquella ocasión, el futbolista también se perdió únicamente un partido, aunque continuó entrenándose con normalidad junto al resto de sus compañeros. Un castigo que, aunque ha conllevado además una multa económica importante, muchos aficionados consideran insuficiente y que mantiene intacta la enorme decepción provocada por el comportamiento del jugador.

articles.title: Romario defiende a Cristiano: "Su error fue no mandar a Jorge Jesus a tomar por culo"
articles.standfirst: El astro brasileño afirma que, si todo ocurrió como ha contado el futbolista luso, él hubiera hecho lo mismo: "Si no cumplió su palabra, actuó de mala fe"
articles.summary: El astro brasileño afirma que, si todo ocurrió como ha contado el futbolista luso, él hubiera hecho lo mismo: "Si no cumplió su palabra, actuó de mala fe"
articles.body: La crisis entre Cristiano Ronaldo y Jorge Jesus sigue generando reacciones en todo el mundo del fútbol. La última ha llegado de la mano de Romario, que salió en defensa del capitán portugués durante una entrevista en el 'Charla Podcast', donde aseguró que entiende perfectamente la decisión de abandonar la concentración de la selección si los hechos ocurrieron tal y como los relató el delantero. El campeón del mundo con Brasil en 1994 comenzó dejando claro que concede credibilidad a la versión ofrecida por Cristiano. "Cristiano me parece una persona muy objetiva", afirmó, antes de referirse a su relación con el actual seleccionador portugués. "Me gusta Jorge Jesus. Tuve relación con él cuando entrenaba al Flamengo. Me encontré con él cinco o seis veces y siempre fue una gran persona". Sin embargo, Romario fue contundente al analizar el origen del conflicto. "Según Cristiano, el seleccionador no cumplió su palabra. Y cuando alguien no cumple su palabra contigo, actúa de mala fe. Si paso lo que dijo Ronaldo, entonces tiene razón". La leyenda brasileña también justificó la marcha de Cristiano de la concentración portuguesa. "Dicen que abandonó la selección. Claro. Ya pasó una humillación una vez. ¿Para qué iba a pasar por una segunda?", señaló. Según el exdelantero, el problema se agravó porque no se respetaron determinados acuerdos previos relacionados con la comparecencia pública del seleccionador. "Habían acordado algunas cosas para que él dijera en la rueda de prensa, y no dijo absolutamente nada. Según Ronaldo, fue arrogante y dejó expuesto a Cristiano". Romario considera que esa situación llevó al portugués al límite. "En esas circunstancias, se sintió una persona desprestigiada, como alguien que ya no tenía ninguna relevancia, y por eso se fue. Yo habría hecho exactamente lo mismo". Fiel a su estilo directo y sin filtros, Romario aseguró que incluso habría ido más lejos que Cristiano: "Antes que nada, habría dado un portazo y me habría marchado. Su error no fue irse. Su error fue no mandar antes a ese tipo a tomar por culo", concluyó.

articles.title: Aubameyang: “Es la primera vez en mi carrera que me lesiono más de diez días”
articles.standfirst: La estrella del Deportivo en este comienzo de temporada está feliz en la ciudad y afirma que volverá pronto y con más fuerzas tras su lesión
articles.summary: La estrella del Deportivo en este comienzo de temporada está feliz en la ciudad y afirma que volverá pronto y con más fuerzas tras su lesión
articles.body: Pierre Emerick Aubameyang sigue recuperándose de su operación de menisco. El gabonés recibió el galardón de mejor jugador del Dépor en este inicio de Liga. “Estoy muy contento, recibí muchos premios en mi carrera, pero este es especial por el cariño de la gente de La Coruña”, ha dicho. El atacante se siente cada día mejor y ya camina sin muletas. “Lo más importante es no sentir molestias en la rodilla y ahora ya empecé con la bicicleta, voy a ir poco a poco y cuando salga al campo veré cuánto falta para volver”, aseguró. El ‘7’ blanquiazul explicó cómo se lesionó y en qué jugada se dio cuenta de que había algo raro. “Fue en una acción del partido ante el Betis, quise salvar una pelota, levanté la pierna y al aterrizar ya sentí que algo estaba mal… Es la primera vez que me lesiono en mi carrera más de diez días. Mentalmente fue duro al principio, pero llegaron mis hermanos de Italia y ya estoy deseando volver”, expresó. Aubameyang, además, se mostró bastante extrañado al ver las diferentes lesiones, poco habituales, de Casadó y Eddahchouri en la clavícula y en la muñeca. “Es muy raro tener lesiones de clavícula, de muñeca, la mía de la rodilla es más habitual pero las otras no… El mejor timing es estar juntos todos. El parón nos vino bien y volveremos mejor seguro”, comentó. La química dentro y fuera del terreno de juego que tienen Auba y Nsongo es grande. En tono gracioso, aseguró que vale por dos delanteros: “Nsongo no tiene que caer en la presión de ser el único delantero ahora, de todas formas Nsongo vale por dos puntas…” (se ríe). El internacional gabonés se siente feliz en la ciudad y contento por haber elegido el Deportivo: “Desde que llegué a la ciudad me acogieron bien a mí y a mi familia. Estoy encantado y, salvo la lesión, el resto fue el aterrizaje soñado”. Aubameyang no podrá estar con sus compañeros en San Sebastián. Y el delantero les pide que traigan los puntos. “El grupo está trabajando bien, se puede ganar el partido y confío mucho en ellos, hay mucha calidad y pueden ganar”, aseguró y confirmó que volverá a hacer las volteretas cuando esté recuperado: “Ahora con mi rodilla nueva tengo que recuperarme y después vendrán más volteretas”.

articles.title: El escudo vuelve a la fachada del Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: Dos meses después de colocar las letras del nombre comercial, el club instalará en el lateral de Castellana el emblema tan reclamado por la afición
articles.summary: Dos meses después de colocar las letras del nombre comercial, el club instalará en el lateral de Castellana el emblema tan reclamado por la afición
articles.body: El rótulo del Santiago Bernabéu está a punto de quedar completo. La próxima semana, si nada se tuerce, el Real Madrid procederá a la instalación del escudo del club en la fachada del estadio, junto a las letras que deletrean el nombre del coliseo. Será el remate de un proceso que arrancó a mediados de agosto y que, hasta ahora, había dejado la imagen a medias. El origen de todo se remonta al pasado 13 de agosto, cuando el club comenzó a colocar las letras de 'Bernabéu' en la fachada de cara al estreno liguero en casa. Aquella instalación, sin embargo, quedó algo escueta. Ni el escudo del Real Madrid ni el logotipo de la marca comercial del estadio llegaron a montarse entonces. El rótulo lucía el nombre del recinto, pero sin el emblema que lo identifica y sin la denominación completa de Santiago Bernabéu. El resultado no dejó satisfecha a buena parte de la afición, que echó en falta tanto el distintivo del club como el nombre íntegro del estadio. La imagen de la fachada, incompleta, generó cierta decepción de los seguidores madridistas, que esperaban ver reflejada en la coraza del nuevo Bernabéu la identidad del club con todos sus símbolos. Esa reclamación tiene ahora respuesta. Durante esta misma semana, los operarios ya han comenzado a trabajar sobre la fachada, realizando un estudio a la altura donde están situadas las letras para preparar la instalación de la estructura que soportará el escudo. El emblema, que superará los cinco metros de altura, seguramente se colocará delante de la palabra 'Bernabéu', completando así el conjunto que la afición reclamaba.

articles.title: Stassin apura sus opciones
articles.standfirst: El belga vuelve a tocar balón sobre el césped y podría llegar a tiempo para visitar al Levante
articles.summary: El belga vuelve a tocar balón sobre el césped y podría llegar a tiempo para visitar al Levante
articles.body: Este jueves, el Sevilla completó una nueva sesión matinal de entrenamientos en la ciudad deportiva, como parte de su preparación para la visita del próximo lunes al Levante en el Ciutat de València. En esta segunda jornada de trabajo de la semana, la mayoría de los focos estuvieron centrados en la figura de Lucas Stassin, que se convirtió en la gran noticia de la mañana. El delantero belga saltó al césped para volver a tocar el balón por primera vez desde que cayera lesionado tras el encuentro ante el Deportivo de la Coruña. A pesar de que Stassin sigue ejercitándose al margen de la plantilla, su proceso de recuperación marcha en consonancia con los plazos marcados por el cuerpo médico, por lo que podría unirse a la dinámica grupal este viernes o, como muy tarde, en la sesión del sábado. De esta forma, ganaría muchas opciones de formar parte de la expedición sevillista que volará este domingo hacia tierras valencianas. Otra de las notas positivas en el conjunto de Luis García Plaza continúa siendo el estado físico de Kike Salas y Rubén Vargas. Ambos futbolistas sumaron un nuevo entrenamiento completo a máxima intensidad junto con el resto de sus compañeros, confirmando así que se encuentran a total disposición y que apuntan directamente a la lista de convocados para el duelo frente al Levante. Los dos internacionales que quedaban por reincorporarse al Sevilla, Gabriel Suazo y Robbie Ure, estuvieron trabajando en el gimnasio de la ciudad deportiva tras su largo periplo con sus combinados nacionales. Con su presencia, Luis García Plaza da por cerrado el éxodo debido al parón de selecciones, a la espera de que poder contar con el chileno y el escocés en las últimas sesiones previas a la octava jornada de LaLiga EA Sports.

articles.title: Rangers: Derek McInnes 'not a fan' of extended break
articles.summary: Rangers manager Derek McInnes says he is "not a fan" of the extended international break which he considers "too long".
articles.body:
Rangers manager Derek McInnes says he is "not a fan" of the extended international break which he considers "too long".

The Ibrox club had 13 players away on duty for their countries after the Scottish Premiership win over Celtic on 20 September.

McInnes says the full squad will only train together on Friday, the day before the visit of Kilmarnock and 19 days after their derby triumph.

"Our players are away with different federations, working with different staff and travelling all over the world for four games," McInnes said.

"It's tough for the players to be away from their families, but equally for us there is a lot of nervousness about your players going into other countries' hands for so long.

"They're all back in today but they're not all training. So by the time we get on to the pitch together tomorrow it'll be 19 days since the Celtic game.

"That's longer than a lot of tournaments for a lot of countries. I know it's set in stone - but I'm not a fan of it to be honest."

Shankland sure lots of games to come by return

Why early-season data points to Premiership style shift

Rangers went into the break on a run of six straight victories, the latest two over Celtic in the League Cup and Premiership.

It was a much-needed revival for McInnes, who was named the Premiership manager of the month for September, and his side after a rocky start to his time at Ibrox which involved an exit from European competition.

The Rangers boss says he is under "no illusions" their good form has to continue, and also revealed he had lunch with Sir Alex Ferguson at the club's training ground.

The former Manchester United boss was a regular visitor to Tynecastle last season as McInnes spearheaded Hearts' unexpected title charge.

"He spent a bit of time with the staff and me, chewing the fat as he does," McInnes explained. "He has always been really supportive, and I'm sure he is with a lot of managers.

"I've had a couple of conversations with him since I've been at the club, but to see him in person was good. Particularly after his health scare.

"He enjoyed what we were doing at Hearts and he was a regular visitor. But he understood the opportunity for me to come here was there and we spoke long and hard about that.

"He spoke about his own difficult starts at Man United, and he said it's how you finish a campaign not how you start the campaign. Sometimes it can take time.

"He thought we were really strong on the performance at Celtic Park in particular."

articles.title: England: Lauren James says Sarina Wiegman's side must have no regrets as Greece World Cup play-off awaits
articles.summary: Lauren James says England cannot change their predicament ahead of their two-legged Women's World Cup qualification play-off with Greece; the Lionesses play Greece away in Crete on Friday, before hosting the same opposition four days later at Leicester's King Power Stadium
articles.body:
England face Greece home and away after finishing second in qualifying Group 3 behind Spain on goal difference.

If they progress past Greece, Sarina Wiegman's side will face the winner of the Slovakia vs Ukraine tie, with the team that comes through that securing qualification for next summer's World Cup in Brazil.

"We can't change what happened and that's where we are now," James told Sky Sports News.

"I think we have to just try to look forward to win these games.

"That's always our goal at the end of the day, and the position we're in at the moment is, we have to win in order to get to somewhere.

"The World Cup's a massive tournament that you always want to be a part of and it's everyone's dream from a little kid.

"So, to go there and get another opportunity again, it's obviously something we're all trying to aim for."

James, who signed a new contract earlier this year, is in good form at club level, with second-placed Chelsea dropping just two points from five league games this season.

But the forward, who was Chelsea's player of the year in 2024, insists her best is still to come.

"I'm always looking forward to coming into camp with England and getting another opportunity to play games for the country," said James.

"I think it always helps massively when you're doing well with your club, which obviously is why you get called up for your country. Hopefully I can just build the momentum and keep going.

"Every time I put on a shirt, whether it's for club or country, I always want to just show what I'm made of.

"The more you play, the more you have rhythm and I like to just play free. And I think the best is still yet to come.

"I'm just trying to enjoy my football and look forward to the things that are coming up."

Potter was 'really surprised' by England call

Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter admits she was "surprised" to earn her first England call-up ahead for the World Cup play-off fixtures.

The 20-year-old has enjoyed a bright start to the campaign after being given a run of starts under Blues boss Sonia Bompastor.

Potter has played a part in all four of Chelsea's victories this season in the Women's Super League and got herself on the scoresheet in a 2-0 win over Birmingham last month.

The youngster learned of her call-up while in her bedroom at her family home, before sharing her delight with her mother.

"I've been really lucky and grateful for the opportunities I've been given at Chelsea and when I got the call, I was really surprised," Potter said.

"I like to stay focused every day and be the best version of myself and don't like to think too far ahead.

"I was at home, I still live at home so I was just in my room watching my phone a bit and then when I got the call I was really happy and went downstairs and told my mum and she was really proud of me."

articles.title: Funes: "Nos ha venido genial el parón, el equipo está loco por jugar"
articles.standfirst: El técnico de Loja analizó el duelo contra el Espanyol
articles.summary: El técnico de Loja analizó el duelo contra el Espanyol
articles.body: El Málaga vuelve a competir. Dos semanas después de su último partido, el conjunto blanquiazul regresa este viernes a La Rosaleda para medirse al Espanyol (21:00 horas) con una cuenta pendiente: conseguir la primera victoria de la temporada. Funes afronta el regreso con varias novedades en su plantilla y con la sensación de que el parón ha servido para ajustar algunas cosas. "Nos han venido genial estas semanas. Muchos jugadores han acumulado minutos y hemos aprovechado los entrenamientos. Nos ha valido para hacer ajustes y prepararnos bien", explicó el técnico malaguista en la previa. Funes reconoce que el equipo necesita dar un paso adelante, especialmente en la presión y en la capacidad para llegar con más velocidad al área rival. "Nos gustaría recuperar más alto y poder llegar más rápido al área rival. Vamos a ver qué podemos hacer para cambiar eso". Una de las grandes noticias está en la convocatoria. Haitam vuelve a estar disponible, mientras que Calero y Adam Aznou estarán también en la lista y podrían estrenarse como jugadores del Málaga. «Calero está en muy buena línea. Aznou probablemente debute ya mañana», confirmó Funes. El marroquí, además, puede ser una alternativa para jugar más arriba durante los partidos, aunque el entrenador no apunta a utilizarlo inicialmente como extremo. También vuelve a estar disponible Chupete, que llega al partido después de su convocatoria con la España Sub-21. "Es un estímulo y siempre son bien recibidos. Seguro que le va a ayudar a sentirse con más confianza", señaló Funes. El caso de Rafita es diferente. El canterano ha acumulado minutos durante el parón, pero llega más justo. "Si hoy fuera el partido, no estaría disponible. Esperemos que pueda entrar mañana en la convocatoria". El Málaga tendrá enfrente a un Espanyol que llega liderado por Roberto Fernández, aunque Funes quiso dejar claro que el peligro perico va mucho más allá del delantero malagueño. "Roberto está en estado de gracia. Los balones que toca se convierten en gol", admitió. Pero también lanzó una advertencia: "Se habla mucho de Roberto, pero tienen más argumentos". El técnico destacó la fortaleza del equipo catalán en los duelos aéreos y su capacidad para generar peligro con pocos acercamientos. Mientras tanto, Jens Cajuste sigue avanzando en su recuperación y ya trabaja con el grupo, aunque todavía necesita tiempo para volver a competir. "Está en la última etapa de recuperación. No es una lesión grave, pero sí ha sido un contratiempo", explicó Funes. El entrenador tampoco descarta cambios en el sistema y reconoció que la defensa de tres es una opción que ya se ha trabajado: "Es una posibilidad real y puede terminar sucediendo".

articles.title: Agoumé: "Fofana me llamó para decirme que había firmado por el Sevilla y no me lo creía"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista francés ha pasado por los micrófonos de Radio MARCA Sevilla
articles.summary: El centrocampista francés ha pasado por los micrófonos de Radio MARCA Sevilla
articles.body: Uno de los líderes del Sevilla de Luis García Plaza es Lucien Agoumé. El centrocampista es el jugador que más se ha revalorizado en el arranque de temporada tanto a nivel deportivo como económico. Un fijo para su entrenador y un activo a tener en cuenta de cara a futuras ventanas de transferencias. El francés ha pasado este mediodía por los micrófonos de Radio MARCA Sevilla. "La gente ve los partidos y lo dice. Seguramente es un momento muy bueno del equipo con los resultados que estamos teniendo y puede ser que la gente le eche más cuenta a lo que hago porque antes no era tan malo", bromeaba el jugador cuestionado por su notable arranque de temporada. "La situación es buena, pero tenemos que seguir trabajando. Competir así es el único camino que tenemos que llevar hasta el final". El apoyo de la grada es fundamental. "Este año se nota que la afición está con nosotros en todos los partidos. Es una afición que aprieta mucho y en casa se nota que con ellos podemos ganar todos los partidos de casa. Nos están dando ese apoyo que nos hace falta para superarnos y este año se nota mucho más, juegan una parte en los resultados que estamos teniendo", afirmó el jugador. Jugar con el ambiente en contra "es incómodo" porque "el fútbol une a mucha gente y no es que no estuvieran con nosotros, pero se quejaban de la situación y eso se nota en el campo. No era miedo, pero este año se nota también fuera que están siempre con nosotros". "Hemos remontado dos o tres veces porque apoyan hasta el final. Lo vimos también en el final de la temporada pasada, cuando más lo necesitábamos, y la salvación la conseguimos entre todos", añadía. Nuevos compañeros. "Algunos llegaron más tarde, pero los que llevamos más tiempo hemos intentado integrarlos rápido en el grupo y se está notando. En el campo se ve el rendimiento y hacen lo que saben hacer. No hay que decirles nada, solo meterles en el grupo, que se sientan bien". García Plaza. "El míster nos pide siempre que compitamos hasta el final y ante cualquier rival, hacerlo siempre de la misma manera. Hay que competir siempre porque cuando lo haces, a veces puedes perder, pero estás siempre más cerca de ganar y es lo que más me llama la atención". Fofana. "Lo veo muy bien. En los pocos partidos que lleva ha mostrado su calidad y lo que nos puede aportar este año. También su experiencia porque lleva bastantes internacionalidades con Francia, cosa que no es fácil. Ha jugado en equipos importantes como el Mónaco, el Milan, y nos está aportando mucho. Jugar con futbolistas así te facilita las cosas". Fofana, fichaje sorpresa. "Cuando firmó, que serían las doce de la noche, no me había enterado todavía de su fichaje y él me llamó para decírmelo, serían las doce y cinco, y no me lo creía. Muy sorprendido pero también muy contento porque nos va a ayudar mucho". Selección francesa. "Es un sueño de todos los niños que empiezan a jugar al fútbol, hacerlo con los mayores pero no me enfoco mucho en eso. Lo único que tengo que hacer es hacer mi trabajo aquí y si tiene que pasar, pasará. Lo más importante es hacer las cosas bien aquí y Francia es un equipo muy potente, con jugadores importantes. A ver qué pasa". Interés de la Premier y la oferta de Arabia Saudí. "Todo lo que me interesa es jugar mi fútbol, disfrutar con los compañeros y ya está". "No fue una decisión complicada, era mucho dinero pero cada uno decide para qué juega al fútbol. Cada año salen posibilidades, ofertas, pero mi idea era seguir aquí. Estoy muy contento de la decisión que tomé y a seguir juntos".

articles.title: Kovac's tough love has Dortmund dreaming of title charge
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovac is defying his critics so far this season, having guided the team to their best start to a Bundesliga campaign in over a d...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovac is defying his critics so far this season, having guided the team to their best start to a Bundesliga campaign in over a decade.

Former Bayern Munich boss Kovac was viewed as an underwhelming choice when he joined Dortmund in January 2025, but the Croatian's no-nonsense, safety-first approach now has the club dreaming of a first league title since 2012.

Dortmund are two points clear of Bayern at the top of the Bundesliga table having won all of their opening four games.

Speaking ahead of his side's home game against Werder Bremen on Friday, Kovac said he was happy to be the frontrunner.

"There's still a very long way to go until we reach the goal that one or two people might have in their head, but we are enjoying this moment," he said Wednesday.

His employers seem equally convinced, with Dortmund CEO, Carsten Cramer, confirming this week that the club intend to extend Kovac's contract.

"The appreciation for Niko Kovac is incredibly big," Cramer told AFP subsidiary SID, adding that it was "only a matter of time" before the coach signed a new deal.

The positivity is all a far cry from Kovac's arrival in Dortmund last year, which prompted raised eyebrows among many fans.

Kovac, who turns 55 next Thursday, was seen as an unglamorous choice following a disappointing spell in charge of Wolfsburg and a fractious tenure at Bayern Munich.

Despite winning the domestic double with Bayern in 2019, Kovac's defensive style and reputation as a disciplinarian saw him clash with big-name players.

Yet those qualities have seen him thrive in Dortmund, transforming a once glass-jawed team into one of the toughest defensive units in the Bundesliga.

After losing four of his first six league games at Dortmund, Kovac ultimately guided the team to Champions League qualification in 2025 and a comfortable second-place finish behind Bayern last season.

The success has been built on his trademark tough-love approach, with a focus on defensive stability, discipline and fitness.

According to German football magazine Kicker, Kovac's motto is "KISS", which stands for "Keep It Simple, Stupid".

"Niko got into the players' heads, gave them clear instructions and created a culture of performance," Dortmund's sporting director Lars Ricken told Kicker.

"For a long time, people used to say that we lacked stability, but Niko has given us that. We are now more physically resilient and we have fewer injuries."

At a club whose modern identity was forged in the "heavy metal football" of Jurgen Klopp, criticism has lingered over Kovac's style of play.

"If I'm honest, it's not my favourite way to play," forward Julian Brandt, who has since moved to Ajax, told Bild newspaper last December.

Yet the Dortmund hierarchy remain convinced that Kovac's back-to-basics approach is what the club and the team need.

"We know that there is an emotional connection to attacking football here in Dortmund, but we can't have fireworks in every game. When you have 50 games a season, dirty wins are just as important," Ricken told Kicker.

For now, few can argue that Kovac's approach has not brought results.

Dortmund have conceded just 1.02 goals on average since Kovac took charge, the lowest rate of any coach since Klopp.

Amid their best start to a season in 11 years, many are asking whether Kovac could become the first man since Klopp to lead Dortmund to the league title.

The coach himself, though, is keeping his feet on the ground.

"We need to keep working hard, keep believing, and stay positive," he said.

articles.title: Time to draw line through Spygate - Parkinson
articles.summary: Wrexham's Phil Parkinson believes it is time to draw a line under Southampton's Spygate scandal following the Football Association (FA)'s verdict.
articles.body:
Wrexham's Phil Parkinson believes it is time to draw a line under the Spygate scandal and has called on the football world to "move on" after the Football Association (FA)'s verdict.

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has been given a six-week suspended ban and a £28,000 fine by the FA for his role in the Spygate scandal.

Parkinson, whose side missed out on the play-off last season before Saints were kicked out of the final for spying on three Championship opponents, expressed his confusion at the length of the investigation.

But the 58-year-old, one of the most senior managers in England's second tier, feels Saints had already paid a heavy enough price, having also been handed a four-point deduction for this season.

"Everybody outside of Southampton [and probably those inside the club] has been concerned about why it has taken so long to get to this point," said Parkinson.

"I can't quite fathom it. Everybody has now got to respect the decision, firstly from the English Football League (EFL) and secondly from the FA.

"They are going to move on, and everybody else has to move on. I was reading the chairman [Dragan Solak]'s quotes. They have been punished severely.

"They lost the chance to get into the Premier League. That is punishment enough. Tonda is a young manager, and I'm sure he has accepted responsibility.

"He will learn from that, but now everybody has to draw a line through it and move on."

Wrexham's Hollywood owners, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, took a dig at Southampton with a promotional video released ahead of their league fixture last month.

The Red Dragons went on to win that meeting 2-1 at the Racecourse, thanks to Keven Schlotterbeck's own goal at the death.

That victory sent Wrexham into the extended international break on a high, and reduced the pressure on Parkinson following a 6-0 defeat at West Ham.

But the triple promotion-winning manager admitted three weeks without a Championship fixture posed new challenges for the club.

"It has been a long three weeks. The three weeks have been decent. The friendly against Wigan was really important," Parkinson added.

"Three weeks is too long for the lads to go without a competitive game. All we could do is plan out the three weeks, which we did.

"I feel, in the main, that we have got [what we wanted]. We have had a few bumps along the way," he added.

"There have been a few things that did not go our way, but everybody is going to get that across a three-week period.

"In general, I feel the lads have trained well. They've had a decent balance of rest, fitness work and 11 vs 11 practice."

articles.title: Missouri announces major update on freshman lineman DJ Jones’ heart transplant
articles.summary: The four-star freshman's heart problem surfaced during summer intake testing.
articles.body:
Missouri Tigers freshman offensive tackle Johnnie "DJ" Jones received a heart transplant and is recovering, the school announced Thursday, two days after coach Eli Drinkwitz fought back tears while revealing the 18-year-old was on a transplant list.

In a statement released Thursday morning , Missouri said, "Last night, DJ received his heart transplant, and his surgery went well. He is now recovering." The letter also thanked the medical staff that cared for Jones and the donor family "whose extraordinary gift made this possible."

Missouri's medical staff detected a heart problem during freshman intake testing this summer. Drinkwitz said the staff monitored the 18-year-old in Columbia for about two weeks without finding a resolution, so the program sent him to the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida, where doctors discovered "a much more significant issue."

"Last week, we found out that Johnnie is now on a heart transplant list," Drinkwitz said Tuesday . "He's in Mayo, and it's tough right now."

Jones arrived in Columbia as the highest-rated signee in Missouri's 2026 recruiting class. 247Sports ranked the four-star prospect as the No. 11 offensive tackle and No. 108 overall player in the cycle.

The 6-foot-6 lineman started at left tackle for Venice High School, which reached its division's championship game during his senior season. He initially committed to UCLA, then chose Missouri over Georgia, Ole Miss, Florida and Florida State before signing in early December.

Jones hasn't appeared in a game this season. A support page organizer, La'Ron Louis, created a page on Oct. 6 and set a $200,000 goal to help the Jones family cover hospital bills, transportation, meals and time away from work during his extended hospital stay.

Missouri Tigers head coach Eliah Drinkwitz reacts from the sideline | William Purnell-Imagn Images

Drinkwitz gave the Venice High School product a shoutout in his on-field postgame interview after Missouri's 45-17 win over then-No. 8 Florida on Saturday, a result SEC Network analyst Paul Finebaum used to rule the Gators out of the College Football Playoff race.

"I know Johnnie was watching our game," Drinkwitz said Tuesday. "But we're praying for him, and I know a lot of Mizzou fans will hopefully join in that prayer, because he does need help in a hurry."

The blowout lifted Missouri 11 spots to No. 14 in the AP Top 25 at 4-1. Texas A&M at Missouri kicks off at noon ET Saturday at Faurot Field on ABC, and Missouri said it will continue to share updates on the freshman tackle's recovery when it can.
